units.leftText: Now there was a certain man of Ramathaim Zophim, of the hill country of Ephraim, and his name was Elkanah, the son of Jeroham, the son of Elihu, the son of Tohu, the son of Zuph, an Ephraimite.
units.rightText: Now there was a man named Elkanah who was from Ramathaim-zophim in the hill country of Ephraim. He was the son of Jeroham, the son of Elihu, the son of Tohu, the son of Zuph, an Ephraimite.
rightNotes: 1:1 Or from Ramathaim, a Zuphite; see LXX and 1 Chronicles 6:26|1CH 6:26* and 35.
1:1 Elihu is also called Eliab and Eliel; see 1 Chronicles 6:27|1CH 6:27* and 34.

units.leftText: He had two wives. The name of one was Hannah, and the name of the other Peninnah. Peninnah had children, but Hannah had no children.
units.rightText: He had two wives, one named Hannah and the other Peninnah. And Peninnah had children, but Hannah had none.

units.leftText: This man went up out of his city from year to year to worship and to sacrifice to the LORD of Armies in Shiloh. The two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, priests to the LORD, were there.
units.rightText: Year after year Elkanah would go up from his city to worship and sacrifice to the LORD of Hosts at Shiloh, where Eli’s two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, were priests to the LORD.
leftNotes: 1:3 When rendered in ALL CAPITAL LETTERS, “LORD” or “GOD” is the translation of God’s Proper Name (Hebrew “יהוה*”, usually pronounced Yahweh).

units.leftText: When the day came that Elkanah sacrificed, he gave portions to Peninnah his wife and to all her sons and her daughters;
units.rightText: And whenever the day came for Elkanah to present his sacrifice, he would give portions to his wife Peninnah and to all her sons and daughters.

units.leftText: but he gave a double portion to Hannah, for he loved Hannah, but the LORD had shut up her womb.
units.rightText: But to Hannah he would give a double portion, for he loved her even though the LORD had closed her womb.
rightNotes: 1:5 Or a choice portion

units.leftText: Her rival provoked her severely, to irritate her, because the LORD had shut up her womb.
units.rightText: Because the LORD had closed Hannah’s womb, her rival would provoke her viciously to taunt her.

units.leftText: So year by year, when she went up to the LORD’s house, her rival provoked her. Therefore she wept, and didn’t eat.
units.rightText: And this went on year after year. Whenever Hannah went up to the house of the LORD, her rival taunted her until she wept and would not eat.

units.leftText: Elkanah her husband said to her, “Hannah, why do you weep? Why don’t you eat? Why is your heart grieved? Am I not better to you than ten sons?”
units.rightText: “Hannah, why are you crying?” her husband Elkanah asked. “Why won’t you eat? Why is your heart so grieved? Am I not better to you than ten sons?”

units.leftText: So Hannah rose up after they had finished eating and drinking in Shiloh. Now Eli the priest was sitting on his seat by the doorpost of the LORD’s temple.
units.rightText: So after they had finished eating and drinking in Shiloh, Hannah stood up. Now Eli the priest was sitting on a chair by the doorpost of the temple of the LORD.

units.leftText: She was in bitterness of soul, and prayed to the LORD, weeping bitterly.
units.rightText: In her bitter distress, Hannah prayed to the LORD and wept with many tears.

units.leftText: She vowed a vow, and said, “LORD of Armies, if you will indeed look at the affliction of your servant and remember me, and not forget your servant, but will give to your servant a boy, then I will give him to the LORD all the days of his life, and no razor shall come on his head.”
units.rightText: And she made a vow, saying, “O LORD of Hosts, if only You will look upon the affliction of Your maidservant and remember me, not forgetting Your maidservant but giving her a son, then I will dedicate him to the LORD all the days of his life, and no razor shall ever touch his head.”

units.leftText: As she continued praying before the LORD, Eli saw her mouth.
units.rightText: As Hannah kept on praying before the LORD, Eli watched her mouth.

units.leftText: Now Hannah spoke in her heart. Only her lips moved, but her voice was not heard. Therefore Eli thought she was drunk.
units.rightText: Hannah was praying in her heart, and though her lips were moving, her voice could not be heard.

units.leftText: Eli said to her, “How long will you be drunk? Get rid of your wine!”
units.rightText: and said to her, “How long will you be drunk? Put away your wine!”

units.leftText: Hannah answered, “No, my lord, I am a woman of a sorrowful spirit. I have not been drinking wine or strong drink, but I poured out my soul before the LORD.
units.rightText: “No, my lord,” Hannah replied. “I am a woman troubled in spirit. I have not had any wine or strong drink, but I have poured out my soul before the LORD.

units.leftText: Don’t consider your servant a wicked woman; for I have been speaking out of the abundance of my complaint and my provocation.”
units.rightText: Do not take your servant for a wicked woman, for all this time I have been praying out of the depth of my anguish and grief.”

units.leftText: Then Eli answered, “Go in peace; and may the God of Israel grant your petition that you have asked of him.”
units.rightText: “Go in peace,” Eli replied, “and may the God of Israel grant the petition you have asked of Him.”
leftNotes: 1:17 The Hebrew word rendered “God” is “אֱלֹהִ֑ים*” (Elohim).

units.leftText: She said, “Let your servant find favor in your sight.” So the woman went her way and ate; and her facial expression wasn’t sad any more.
units.rightText: “May your maidservant find favor with you,” said Hannah. Then she went on her way, and she began to eat, and her face was no longer downcast.

units.leftText: They rose up in the morning early and worshiped the LORD, then returned and came to their house to Ramah. Then Elkanah knew Hannah his wife; and the LORD remembered her.
units.rightText: The next morning they got up early to bow in worship before the LORD, and then they returned home to Ramah.

units.leftText: When the time had come, Hannah conceived, and bore a son; and she named him Samuel, saying, “Because I have asked him of the LORD.”
units.rightText: So in the course of time, Hannah conceived and gave birth to a son. She named him Samuel, saying, “Because I have asked for him from the LORD.”
leftNotes: 1:20 Samuel sounds like the Hebrew for “heard by God.”
rightNotes: 1:20 Samuel sounds like the Hebrew for heard of God.

units.leftText: The man Elkanah, and all his house, went up to offer to the LORD the yearly sacrifice and his vow.
units.rightText: Then Elkanah and all his house went up to make the annual sacrifice to the LORD and to fulfill his vow,

units.leftText: But Hannah didn’t go up, for she said to her husband, “Not until the child is weaned; then I will bring him, that he may appear before the LORD, and stay there forever.”
units.rightText: but Hannah did not go. “After the boy is weaned,” she said to her husband, “I will take him to appear before the LORD and to stay there permanently.”
rightNotes: 1:22 MT; DSS include I will offer him as a Nazirite for all time.

units.leftText: Elkanah her husband said to her, “Do what seems good to you. Wait until you have weaned him; only may the LORD establish his word.”
units.rightText: “Do what you think is best,” her husband Elkanah replied, “and stay here until you have weaned him. Only may the LORD confirm His word.”
rightNotes: 1:23 MT; DSS, LXX, and Syriac your word

units.leftText: When she had weaned him, she took him up with her, with three bulls, and one ephah of meal, and a container of wine, and brought him to the LORD’s house in Shiloh. The child was young.
units.rightText: Once she had weaned him, Hannah took the boy with her, along with a three-year-old bull, an ephah of flour, and a skin of wine. Though the boy was still young, she brought him to the house of the LORD at Shiloh.
leftNotes: 1:24 1 ephah is about 22 liters or about 2/3 of a bushel
rightNotes: 1:24 DSS, LXX, and Syriac; MT three bulls
1:24 An ephah is approximately 20 dry quarts or 22 liters (probably about 25.5 pounds or 11.6 kilograms of flour).

units.leftText: They killed the bull, and brought the child to Eli.
units.rightText: And when they had slaughtered the bull, they brought the boy to Eli.

units.leftText: She said, “Oh, my lord, as your soul lives, my lord, I am the woman who stood by you here, praying to the LORD.
units.rightText: “Please, my lord,” said Hannah, “as surely as you live, my lord, I am the woman who stood here beside you praying to the LORD.

units.leftText: I prayed for this child, and the LORD has given me my petition which I asked of him.
units.rightText: I prayed for this boy, and since the LORD has granted me what I asked of Him,

units.leftText: Therefore I have also given him to the LORD. As long as he lives he is given to the LORD.” He worshiped the LORD there.
units.rightText: I now dedicate the boy to the LORD. For as long as he lives, he is dedicated to the LORD.”

units.leftText: Hannah prayed, and said,
units.rightText: At that time Hannah prayed:

units.leftText: There is no one as holy as the LORD,
units.rightText: There is no one holy like the LORD.

units.leftText: “Don’t keep talking so exceedingly proudly.
units.rightText: Do not boast so proudly,

units.leftText: “The bows of the mighty men are broken.
units.rightText: The bows of the mighty are broken,

units.leftText: Those who were full have hired themselves out for bread.
units.rightText: The well-fed hire themselves out for food,

units.leftText: “The LORD kills and makes alive.
units.rightText: The LORD brings death and gives life;

units.leftText: The LORD makes poor and makes rich.
units.rightText: The LORD sends poverty and wealth;

units.leftText: He raises up the poor out of the dust.
units.rightText: He raises the poor from the dust

units.leftText: He will keep the feet of his holy ones,
units.rightText: He guards the steps of His faithful ones,

units.leftText: Those who strive with the LORD shall be broken to pieces.
units.rightText: Those who oppose the LORD will be shattered.

units.leftText: Elkanah went to Ramah to his house. The child served the LORD before Eli the priest.
units.rightText: Then Elkanah went home to Ramah, but the boy began ministering to the LORD before Eli the priest.

units.leftText: Now the sons of Eli were wicked men. They didn’t know the LORD.
units.rightText: Now the sons of Eli were wicked men; they had no regard for the LORD

units.leftText: The custom of the priests with the people was that when anyone offered a sacrifice, the priest’s servant came while the meat was boiling, with a fork of three teeth in his hand;
units.rightText: or for the custom of the priests with the people.

units.leftText: and he stabbed it into the pan, or kettle, or cauldron, or pot. The priest took all that the fork brought up for himself. They did this to all the Israelites who came there to Shiloh.
units.rightText: and plunge it into the pan or kettle or cauldron or cooking pot. And the priest would claim for himself whatever the meat fork brought up. This is how they treated all the Israelites who came to Shiloh.

units.leftText: Yes, before they burned the fat, the priest’s servant came, and said to the man who sacrificed, “Give meat to roast for the priest; for he will not accept boiled meat from you, but raw.”
units.rightText: Even before the fat was burned, the servant of the priest would come and say to the man who was sacrificing, “Give the priest some meat to roast, because he will not accept boiled meat from you, but only raw.”

units.leftText: If the man said to him, “Let the fat be burned first, and then take as much as your soul desires;” then he would say, “No, but you shall give it to me now; and if not, I will take it by force.”
units.rightText: And if any man said to him, “The fat must be burned first; then you may take whatever you want,” the servant would reply, “No, you must give it to me right now. If you refuse, I will take it by force!”

units.leftText: The sin of the young men was very great before the LORD; for the men despised the LORD’s offering.
units.rightText: Thus the sin of these young men was severe in the sight of the LORD, for they were treating the LORD’s offering with contempt.
rightNotes: 2:17 DSS and LXX; MT men

units.leftText: But Samuel ministered before the LORD, being a child, clothed with a linen ephod.
units.rightText: Now Samuel was ministering before the LORD — a boy wearing a linen ephod.

units.leftText: Moreover his mother made him a little robe, and brought it to him from year to year when she came up with her husband to offer the yearly sacrifice.
units.rightText: Each year his mother would make him a little robe and bring it to him when she went with her husband to offer the annual sacrifice.

units.leftText: Eli blessed Elkanah and his wife, and said, “May the LORD give you offspring from this woman for the petition which was asked of the LORD.” Then they went to their own home.
units.rightText: And Eli would bless Elkanah and his wife, saying, “May the LORD give you children by this woman in place of the one she dedicated to the LORD. ” Then they would go home.
leftNotes: 2:20 or, seed
rightNotes: 2:20 DSS; MT in place of the one requested from the LORD

units.leftText: The LORD visited Hannah, and she conceived and bore three sons and two daughters. The child Samuel grew before the LORD.
units.rightText: So the LORD attended to Hannah, and she conceived and gave birth to three sons and two daughters.

units.leftText: Now Eli was very old; and he heard all that his sons did to all Israel, and how that they slept with the women who served at the door of the Tent of Meeting.
units.rightText: Now Eli was very old, and he heard about everything his sons were doing to all Israel and how they were sleeping with the women who served at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.

units.leftText: He said to them, “Why do you do such things? For I hear of your evil dealings from all these people.
units.rightText: “Why are you doing these things?” Eli said to his sons. “I hear about your wicked deeds from all these people.

units.leftText: No, my sons; for it is not a good report that I hear! You make the LORD’s people disobey.
units.rightText: No, my sons; it is not a good report I hear circulating among the LORD’s people.

units.leftText: If one man sins against another, God will judge him; but if a man sins against the LORD, who will intercede for him?” Notwithstanding, they didn’t listen to the voice of their father, because the LORD intended to kill them.
units.rightText: If a man sins against another man, God can intercede for him; but if a man sins against the LORD, who can intercede for him?”
rightNotes: 2:25 Or the judges

units.leftText: The child Samuel grew on, and increased in favor both with the LORD and also with men.
units.rightText: And the boy Samuel continued to grow in stature and in favor with the LORD and with man.

units.leftText: A man of God came to Eli and said to him, “The LORD says, ‘Did I reveal myself to the house of your father when they were in Egypt in bondage to Pharaoh’s house?
units.rightText: Then a man of God came to Eli and told him, “This is what the LORD says: ‘Did I not clearly reveal Myself to your father’s house when they were in Egypt under Pharaoh’s house?

units.leftText: Didn’t I choose him out of all the tribes of Israel to be my priest, to go up to my altar, to burn incense, to wear an ephod before me? Didn’t I give to the house of your father all the offerings of the children of Israel made by fire?
units.rightText: And out of all the tribes of Israel I selected your father to be My priest, to offer sacrifices on My altar, to burn incense, and to wear an ephod in My presence. I also gave to the house of your father all the food offerings of the Israelites.

units.leftText: Why do you kick at my sacrifice and at my offering, which I have commanded in my habitation, and honor your sons above me, to make yourselves fat with the best of all the offerings of Israel my people?’
units.rightText: Why then do you kick at My sacrifice and offering that I have prescribed for My dwelling place? You have honored your sons more than Me by fattening yourselves with the best of all the offerings of My people Israel.’
rightNotes: 2:29 Or scorn

units.leftText: “Therefore the LORD, the God of Israel, says, ‘I said indeed that your house and the house of your father should walk before me forever.’ But now the LORD says, ‘Far be it from me; for those who honor me I will honor, and those who despise me will be cursed.
units.rightText: Therefore, the LORD, the God of Israel, declares:

units.leftText: Behold, the days come that I will cut off your arm and the arm of your father’s house, that there will not be an old man in your house.
units.rightText: Behold, the days are coming when I will cut off your strength and the strength of your father’s house, so that no one in it will reach old age.
leftNotes: 2:31 “Behold”, from “הִנֵּה*”, means look at, take notice, observe, see, or gaze at. It is often used as an interjection.

units.leftText: You will see the affliction of my habitation, in all the wealth which I will give Israel. There shall not be an old man in your house forever.
units.rightText: You will see distress in My dwelling place. Despite all that is good in Israel, no one in your house will ever again reach old age.

units.leftText: The man of yours whom I don’t cut off from my altar will consume your eyes and grieve your heart. All the increase of your house will die in the flower of their age.
units.rightText: And every one of you that I do not cut off from My altar, I will cause your eyes to fail and your heart to grieve. All your descendants will die by the sword of men.
leftNotes: 2:33 or, blind your eyes with tears
rightNotes: 2:33 Hebrew; LXX his eyes will fail and his heart will grieve
2:33 Or increase
2:33 DSS and LXX; MT will die as mortals or will die in the prime of life

units.leftText: This will be the sign to you that will come on your two sons, on Hophni and Phinehas: in one day they will both die.
units.rightText: And this sign shall come to you concerning your two sons Hophni and Phinehas: They will both die on the same day.

units.leftText: I will raise up a faithful priest for myself who will do according to that which is in my heart and in my mind. I will build him a sure house. He will walk before my anointed forever.
units.rightText: Then I will raise up for Myself a faithful priest. He will do whatever is in My heart and mind. And I will build for him an enduring house, and he will walk before My anointed one for all time.

units.leftText: It will happen that everyone who is left in your house will come and bow down to him for a piece of silver and a loaf of bread, and will say, “Please put me into one of the priests’ offices, that I may eat a morsel of bread.”’”
units.rightText: And everyone left in your house will come and bow down to him for a piece of silver or a morsel of bread, pleading, “Please appoint me to some priestly office so that I can eat a piece of bread.”’”

units.leftText: The child Samuel ministered to the LORD before Eli. The LORD’s word was rare in those days. There were not many visions, then.
units.rightText: And the boy Samuel ministered to the LORD before Eli.

units.leftText: At that time, when Eli was laid down in his place (now his eyes had begun to grow dim, so that he could not see),
units.rightText: And at that time Eli, whose eyesight had grown so dim that he could not see, was lying in his room.

units.leftText: and God’s lamp hadn’t yet gone out, and Samuel had laid down in the LORD’s temple where God’s ark was,
units.rightText: Before the lamp of God had gone out, Samuel was lying down in the temple of the LORD, where the ark of God was located.

units.leftText: The LORD called Samuel. He said, “Here I am.”
units.rightText: Then the LORD called to Samuel, and he answered, “Here I am.”

units.leftText: He ran to Eli and said, “Here I am; for you called me.”
units.rightText: He ran to Eli and said, “Here I am, for you have called me.”

units.leftText: The LORD called yet again, “Samuel!”
units.rightText: Once again the LORD called, “Samuel!”

units.leftText: Now Samuel didn’t yet know the LORD, neither was the LORD’s word yet revealed to him.
units.rightText: Now Samuel did not yet know the LORD, because the word of the LORD had not yet been revealed to him.

units.leftText: The LORD called Samuel again the third time. He arose and went to Eli and said, “Here I am; for you called me.”
units.rightText: Once again, for the third time, the LORD called to Samuel. He got up, went to Eli, and said, “Here I am, for you have called me.”

units.leftText: Therefore Eli said to Samuel, “Go, lie down. It shall be, if he calls you, that you shall say, ‘Speak, LORD; for your servant hears.’” So Samuel went and lay down in his place.
units.rightText: “Go and lie down,” he said to Samuel, “and if He calls you, say, ‘Speak, LORD, for Your servant is listening.’”

units.leftText: The LORD came, and stood, and called as at other times, “Samuel! Samuel!”
units.rightText: Then the LORD came and stood there, calling as before, “Samuel! Samuel!”

units.leftText: The LORD said to Samuel, “Behold, I will do a thing in Israel at which both the ears of everyone who hears it will tingle.
units.rightText: Then the LORD said to Samuel, “I am about to do something in Israel at which the ears of all who hear it will tingle.

units.leftText: In that day I will perform against Eli all that I have spoken concerning his house, from the beginning even to the end.
units.rightText: On that day I will carry out against Eli everything I have spoken about his house, from beginning to end.

units.leftText: For I have told him that I will judge his house forever for the iniquity which he knew, because his sons brought a curse on themselves, and he didn’t restrain them.
units.rightText: I told him that I would judge his house forever for the iniquity of which he knows, because his sons blasphemed God and he did not restrain them.
rightNotes: 3:13 LXX; Hebrew made themselves contemptible

units.leftText: Therefore I have sworn to the house of Eli that the iniquity of Eli’s house shall not be removed with sacrifice or offering forever.”
units.rightText: Therefore I have sworn to the house of Eli, ‘The iniquity of Eli’s house shall never be atoned for by sacrifice or offering.’”

units.leftText: Samuel lay until the morning, and opened the doors of the LORD’s house. Samuel was afraid to show Eli the vision.
units.rightText: Samuel lay down until the morning; then he opened the doors of the house of the LORD. He was afraid to tell Eli the vision,

units.leftText: Then Eli called Samuel and said, “Samuel, my son!”
units.rightText: but Eli called to him and said, “Samuel, my son.”

units.leftText: He said, “What is the thing that he has spoken to you? Please don’t hide it from me. God do so to you, and more also, if you hide anything from me of all the things that he spoke to you.”
units.rightText: “What was the message He gave you?” Eli asked. “Do not hide it from me. May God punish you, and ever so severely, if you hide from me anything He said to you.”

units.leftText: Samuel told him every bit, and hid nothing from him.
units.rightText: So Samuel told him everything and did not hide a thing from him.

units.leftText: Samuel grew, and the LORD was with him and let none of his words fall to the ground.
units.rightText: And Samuel grew, and the LORD was with him, and He let none of Samuel’s words fall to the ground.

units.leftText: All Israel from Dan even to Beersheba knew that Samuel was established to be a prophet of the LORD.
units.rightText: So all Israel from Dan to Beersheba knew that Samuel was confirmed as a prophet of the LORD.

units.leftText: The LORD appeared again in Shiloh; for the LORD revealed himself to Samuel in Shiloh by the LORD’s word.
units.rightText: And the LORD continued to appear at Shiloh, because there He revealed Himself to Samuel by His word.

units.leftText: The word of Samuel came to all Israel.
units.rightText: Thus the word of Samuel came to all Israel.

units.leftText: The Philistines put themselves in array against Israel. When they joined battle, Israel was defeated by the Philistines, who killed about four thousand men of the army in the field.
units.rightText: The Philistines arrayed themselves against Israel, and as the battle spread, Israel was defeated by the Philistines, who struck down about four thousand men on the battlefield.

units.leftText: When the people had come into the camp, the elders of Israel said, “Why has the LORD defeated us today before the Philistines? Let’s get the ark of the LORD’s covenant out of Shiloh and bring it to us, that it may come among us and save us out of the hand of our enemies.”
units.rightText: When the troops returned to the camp, the elders of Israel asked, “Why has the LORD brought defeat on us before the Philistines today? Let us bring the ark of the covenant of the LORD from Shiloh, so that it may go with us to save us from the hand of our enemies.”
rightNotes: 4:3 Or He may go

units.leftText: So the people sent to Shiloh, and they brought from there the ark of the covenant of the LORD of Armies, who sits above the cherubim; and the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were there with the ark of the covenant of God.
units.rightText: So the people sent men to Shiloh, and they brought back the ark of the covenant of the LORD of Hosts, who sits enthroned between the cherubim. And the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were there with the ark of the covenant of God.

units.leftText: When the ark of the LORD’s covenant came into the camp, all Israel shouted with a great shout, so that the earth resounded.
units.rightText: When the ark of the covenant of the LORD entered the camp, all the Israelites raised such a great shout that the ground shook.

units.leftText: When the Philistines heard the noise of the shout, they said, “What does the noise of this great shout in the camp of the Hebrews mean?” They understood that the LORD’s ark had come into the camp.
units.rightText: On hearing the noise of the shout, the Philistines asked, “What is this loud shouting in the camp of the Hebrews?”

units.leftText: The Philistines were afraid, for they said, “God has come into the camp.” They said, “Woe to us! For there has not been such a thing before.
units.rightText: the Philistines were afraid. “The gods have entered their camp!” they said. “Woe to us, for nothing like this has happened before.
rightNotes: 4:7 Or A god has entered

units.leftText: Woe to us! Who shall deliver us out of the hand of these mighty gods? These are the gods that struck the Egyptians with all kinds of plagues in the wilderness.
units.rightText: Woe to us! Who will deliver us from the hand of these mighty gods? These are the gods who struck the Egyptians with all kinds of plagues in the wilderness.

units.leftText: Be strong and behave like men, O you Philistines, that you not be servants to the Hebrews, as they have been to you. Strengthen yourselves like men, and fight!”
units.rightText: Take courage and be men, O Philistines! Otherwise, you will serve the Hebrews just as they served you. Now be men and fight!”

units.leftText: The Philistines fought, and Israel was defeated, and each man fled to his tent. There was a very great slaughter; for thirty thousand footmen of Israel fell.
units.rightText: So the Philistines fought, and Israel was defeated, and each man fled to his tent. The slaughter was very great — thirty thousand foot soldiers of Israel fell.

units.leftText: God’s ark was taken; and the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were slain.
units.rightText: The ark of God was captured, and Eli’s two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, died.

units.leftText: A man of Benjamin ran out of the army and came to Shiloh the same day, with his clothes torn and with dirt on his head.
units.rightText: That same day a Benjamite ran from the battle line all the way to Shiloh, with his clothes torn and dirt on his head.

units.leftText: When he came, behold, Eli was sitting on his seat by the road watching, for his heart trembled for God’s ark. When the man came into the city and told about it, all the city cried out.
units.rightText: When he arrived, there was Eli, sitting on his chair beside the road and watching, because his heart trembled for the ark of God.

units.leftText: When Eli heard the noise of the crying, he said, “What does the noise of this tumult mean?”
units.rightText: Eli heard the outcry and asked, “Why this commotion?”

units.leftText: Now Eli was ninety-eight years old. His eyes were set, so that he could not see.
units.rightText: Now Eli was ninety-eight years old, and his gaze was fixed because he could not see.

units.leftText: The man said to Eli, “I am he who came out of the army, and I fled today out of the army.”
units.rightText: “I have just come from the battle,” the man said to Eli. “I fled from there today.”

units.leftText: He who brought the news answered, “Israel has fled before the Philistines, and there has been also a great slaughter among the people. Your two sons also, Hophni and Phinehas, are dead, and God’s ark has been captured.”
units.rightText: The messenger answered, “Israel has fled before the Philistines, and there has been a great slaughter among the people. Your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, are both dead, and the ark of God has been captured.”

units.leftText: When he made mention of God’s ark, Eli fell from off his seat backward by the side of the gate; and his neck broke, and he died, for he was an old man and heavy. He had judged Israel forty years.
units.rightText: As soon as the ark of God was mentioned, Eli fell backward from his chair by the city gate, and being old and heavy, he broke his neck and died. And Eli had judged Israel forty years.
rightNotes: 4:18 Or governed or led

units.leftText: His daughter-in-law, Phinehas’ wife, was with child, near to giving birth. When she heard the news that God’s ark was taken and that her father-in-law and her husband were dead, she bowed herself and gave birth; for her pains came on her.
units.rightText: Now Eli’s daughter-in-law, the wife of Phinehas, was pregnant and about to give birth. When she heard the news of the capture of God’s ark and the deaths of her father-in-law and her husband, she collapsed and gave birth, for her labor pains overtook her.

units.leftText: About the time of her death the women who stood by her said to her, “Don’t be afraid, for you have given birth to a son.” But she didn’t answer, neither did she regard it.
units.rightText: As she was dying, the women attending to her said, “Do not be afraid, for you have given birth to a son!”

units.leftText: She named the child Ichabod, saying, “The glory has departed from Israel!” because God’s ark was taken, and because of her father-in-law and her husband.
units.rightText: And she named the boy Ichabod, saying, “The glory has departed from Israel,” because the ark of God had been captured and her father-in-law and her husband had been killed.
leftNotes: 4:21 “Ichabod” means “no glory”.
rightNotes: 4:21 Ichabod means no glory.
4:21 Or gone into exile; also in verse 22

units.leftText: She said, “The glory has departed from Israel; for God’s ark has been taken.”
units.rightText: “The glory has departed from Israel,” she said, “for the ark of God has been captured.”

units.leftText: Now the Philistines had taken God’s ark, and they brought it from Ebenezer to Ashdod.
units.rightText: After the Philistines had captured the ark of God, they took it from Ebenezer to Ashdod,

units.leftText: The Philistines took God’s ark, and brought it into the house of Dagon and set it by Dagon.
units.rightText: carried it into the temple of Dagon, and set it beside his statue.
rightNotes: 5:2 Literally set it beside Dagon

units.leftText: When the people of Ashdod arose early on the next day, behold, Dagon had fallen on his face to the ground before the LORD’s ark. They took Dagon and set him in his place again.
units.rightText: When the people of Ashdod got up early the next morning, there was Dagon, fallen on his face before the ark of the LORD. So they took Dagon and returned him to his place.

units.leftText: When they arose early on the following morning, behold, Dagon had fallen on his face to the ground before the LORD’s ark; and the head of Dagon and both the palms of his hands were cut off on the threshold. Only Dagon’s torso was intact.
units.rightText: But when they got up early the next morning, there was Dagon, fallen on his face before the ark of the LORD, with his head and his hands broken off and lying on the threshold. Only the torso remained.

units.leftText: Therefore neither the priests of Dagon nor any who come into Dagon’s house step on the threshold of Dagon in Ashdod to this day.
units.rightText: That is why, to this day, the priests of Dagon and all who enter the temple of Dagon in Ashdod do not step on the threshold.

units.leftText: But the LORD’s hand was heavy on the people of Ashdod, and he destroyed them and struck them with tumors, even Ashdod and its borders.
units.rightText: Now the hand of the LORD was heavy on the people of Ashdod and its vicinity, ravaging them and afflicting them with tumors.
rightNotes: 5:6 Hebrew; LXX and Vulgate include And rats appeared in their land, and death and destruction were throughout the city.

units.leftText: When the men of Ashdod saw that it was so, they said, “The ark of the God of Israel shall not stay with us, for his hand is severe on us and on Dagon our god.”
units.rightText: And when the men of Ashdod saw what was happening, they said, “The ark of the God of Israel must not stay here with us, because His hand is heavy upon us and upon our god Dagon.”

units.leftText: They sent therefore and gathered together all the lords of the Philistines, and said, “What shall we do with the ark of the God of Israel?”
units.rightText: So they called together all the rulers of the Philistines and asked, “What shall we do with the ark of the God of Israel?”

units.leftText: It was so, that after they had carried it there, the LORD’s hand was against the city with a very great confusion; and he struck the men of the city, both small and great, so that tumors broke out on them.
units.rightText: But after they had moved the ark to Gath, the LORD’s hand was also against that city, throwing it into great confusion and afflicting the men of the city, both young and old, with an outbreak of tumors.

units.leftText: So they sent God’s ark to Ekron.
units.rightText: So they sent the ark of God to Ekron, but as it arrived, the Ekronites cried out, “They have brought us the ark of the God of Israel in order to kill us and our people!”

units.leftText: They sent therefore and gathered together all the lords of the Philistines, and they said, “Send the ark of the God of Israel away, and let it go again to its own place, that it not kill us and our people.” For there was a deadly panic throughout all the city. The hand of God was very heavy there.
units.rightText: Then the Ekronites called together all the rulers of the Philistines and said, “Send away the ark of the God of Israel. It must return to its place, so that it will not kill us and our people!”
rightNotes: 5:11 Or He will not

units.leftText: The men who didn’t die were struck with the tumors; and the cry of the city went up to heaven.
units.rightText: Those who did not die were afflicted with tumors, and the outcry of the city went up to heaven.

units.leftText: The LORD’s ark was in the country of the Philistines seven months.
units.rightText: When the ark of the LORD had been in the land of the Philistines seven months,

units.leftText: The Philistines called for the priests and the diviners, saying, “What shall we do with the LORD’s ark? Show us how we should send it to its place.”
units.rightText: the Philistines summoned the priests and diviners, saying, “What shall we do with the ark of the LORD? Tell us how to send it back to its place.”

units.leftText: They said, “If you send away the ark of the God of Israel, don’t send it empty; but by all means return a trespass offering to him. Then you will be healed, and it will be known to you why his hand is not removed from you.”
units.rightText: They replied, “If you return the ark of the God of Israel, do not send it away empty, but by all means return it to Him with a guilt offering. Then you will be healed, and you will understand why His hand has not been lifted from you.”

units.leftText: Then they said, “What should the trespass offering be which we shall return to him?”
units.rightText: “What guilt offering should we send back to Him?” asked the Philistines.

units.leftText: Therefore you shall make images of your tumors and images of your mice that mar the land; and you shall give glory to the God of Israel. Perhaps he will release his hand from you, from your gods, and from your land.
units.rightText: Make images of your tumors and of the rats that are ravaging the land. Give glory to the God of Israel, and perhaps He will lift His hand from you and your gods and your land.

units.leftText: Why then do you harden your hearts as the Egyptians and Pharaoh hardened their hearts? When he had worked wonderfully among them, didn’t they let the people go, and they departed?
units.rightText: Why harden your hearts as the Egyptians and Pharaoh hardened theirs? When He afflicted them, did they not send the people out so they could go on their way?
rightNotes: 6:6 Or make heavy; similarly again in this verse

units.leftText: “Now therefore take and prepare yourselves a new cart and two milk cows on which there has come no yoke; and tie the cows to the cart, and bring their calves home from them;
units.rightText: Now, therefore, prepare one new cart with two milk cows that have never been yoked. Hitch the cows to the cart, but take their calves away and pen them up.

units.leftText: and take the LORD’s ark and lay it on the cart. Put the jewels of gold, which you return him for a trespass offering, in a box by its side; and send it away, that it may go.
units.rightText: Take the ark of the LORD, set it on the cart, and in a chest beside it put the gold objects you are sending back to Him as a guilt offering.

units.leftText: Behold, if it goes up by the way of its own border to Beth Shemesh, then he has done us this great evil; but if not, then we shall know that it is not his hand that struck us. It was a chance that happened to us.”
units.rightText: but keep watching it. If it goes up the road to its homeland, toward Beth-shemesh, it is the LORD who has brought on us this great disaster. But if it does not, then we will know that it was not His hand that punished us and that it happened by chance.”

units.leftText: The men did so, and took two milk cows and tied them to the cart, and shut up their calves at home.
units.rightText: So the men did as instructed. They took two milk cows, hitched them to the cart, and penned up their calves.

units.leftText: They put the LORD’s ark on the cart, and the box with the golden mice and the images of their tumors.
units.rightText: Then they put the ark of the LORD on the cart, along with the chest containing the gold rats and the images of the tumors.

units.leftText: The cows took the straight way by the way to Beth Shemesh. They went along the highway, lowing as they went, and didn’t turn away to the right hand or to the left; and the lords of the Philistines went after them to the border of Beth Shemesh.
units.rightText: And the cows headed straight up the road toward Beth-shemesh, staying on that one highway and lowing as they went, never straying to the right or to the left. The rulers of the Philistines followed behind them to the border of Beth-shemesh.

units.leftText: The people of Beth Shemesh were reaping their wheat harvest in the valley; and they lifted up their eyes and saw the ark, and rejoiced to see it.
units.rightText: Now the people of Beth-shemesh were harvesting wheat in the valley, and when they looked up and saw the ark, they were overjoyed at the sight.

units.leftText: The cart came into the field of Joshua of Beth Shemesh, and stood there, where there was a great stone. Then they split the wood of the cart and offered up the cows for a burnt offering to the LORD.
units.rightText: The cart came to the field of Joshua of Beth-shemesh and stopped there near a large rock. The people chopped up the cart and offered the cows as a burnt offering to the LORD.

units.leftText: The Levites took down the LORD’s ark and the box that was with it, in which the jewels of gold were, and put them on the great stone; and the men of Beth Shemesh offered burnt offerings and sacrificed sacrifices the same day to the LORD.
units.rightText: And the Levites took down the ark of the LORD and the chest containing the gold objects, and they placed them on the large rock. That day the men of Beth-shemesh offered burnt offerings and made sacrifices to the LORD.

units.leftText: When the five lords of the Philistines had seen it, they returned to Ekron the same day.
units.rightText: And when the five rulers of the Philistines saw this, they returned to Ekron that same day.

units.leftText: These are the golden tumors which the Philistines returned for a trespass offering to the LORD: for Ashdod one, for Gaza one, for Ashkelon one, for Gath one, for Ekron one;
units.rightText: As a guilt offering to the LORD, the Philistines had sent back one gold tumor for each city: Ashdod, Gaza, Ashkelon, Gath, and Ekron.

units.leftText: and the golden mice, according to the number of all the cities of the Philistines belonging to the five lords, both of fortified cities and of country villages, even to the great stone on which they set down the LORD’s ark. That stone remains to this day in the field of Joshua of Beth Shemesh.
units.rightText: The number of gold rats also corresponded to the number of Philistine cities belonging to the five rulers — the fortified cities and their outlying villages. And the large rock on which they placed the ark of the LORD stands to this day in the field of Joshua of Beth-shemesh.
rightNotes: 6:18 Or great meadow; Hebrew Abel-haggedolah

units.leftText: He struck of the men of Beth Shemesh, because they had looked into the LORD’s ark, he struck fifty thousand seventy of the men. Then the people mourned, because the LORD had struck the people with a great slaughter.
units.rightText: But God struck down some of the people of Beth-shemesh because they looked inside the ark of the LORD. He struck down seventy men, and the people mourned because the LORD had struck them with a great slaughter.
rightNotes: 6:19 A few late Hebrew manuscripts and Josephus; most Hebrew manuscripts 70 men and 50,000 men; LXX 70 men and 50,000 men of the people; Syriac and Arabic 70 men and 5,000 men; alternately, possibly 70 men and 50 oxen

units.leftText: The men of Beth Shemesh said, “Who is able to stand before the LORD, this holy God? To whom shall he go up from us?”
units.rightText: The men of Beth-shemesh asked, “Who can stand in the presence of the LORD, this holy God? To whom should the ark go up from here?”

units.leftText: They sent messengers to the inhabitants of Kiriath Jearim, saying, “The Philistines have brought back the LORD’s ark. Come down and bring it up to yourselves.”
units.rightText: So they sent messengers to the people of Kiriath-jearim, saying, “The Philistines have returned the ark of the LORD. Come down and take it up with you.”

units.leftText: The men of Kiriath Jearim came and took the LORD’s ark, and brought it into Abinadab’s house on the hill, and consecrated Eleazar his son to keep the LORD’s ark.
units.rightText: Then the men of Kiriath-jearim came for the ark of the LORD and took it into Abinadab’s house on the hill. And they consecrated his son Eleazar to guard the ark of the LORD.

units.leftText: From the day that the ark stayed in Kiriath Jearim, the time was long—for it was twenty years; and all the house of Israel lamented after the LORD.
units.rightText: And from that day a long time passed, twenty years in all, as the ark remained at Kiriath-jearim. And all the house of Israel mournfully sought the LORD.

units.leftText: Samuel spoke to all the house of Israel, saying, “If you are returning to the LORD with all your heart, then put away the foreign gods and the Ashtaroth from among you, and direct your hearts to the LORD, and serve him only; and he will deliver you out of the hand of the Philistines.”
units.rightText: Then Samuel said to all the house of Israel, “If you are returning to the LORD with all your hearts, then put away the foreign gods and Ashtoreths among you, prepare your hearts for the LORD, and serve Him only. And He will deliver you from the hand of the Philistines.”

units.leftText: Then the children of Israel removed the Baals and the Ashtaroth, and served the LORD only.
units.rightText: So the Israelites put away the Baals and Ashtoreths and served only the LORD.

units.leftText: Samuel said, “Gather all Israel to Mizpah, and I will pray to the LORD for you.”
units.rightText: Then Samuel said, “Gather all Israel to Mizpah, and I will pray to the LORD on your behalf.”

units.leftText: They gathered together to Mizpah, and drew water, and poured it out before the LORD, and fasted on that day, and said there, “We have sinned against the LORD.” Samuel judged the children of Israel in Mizpah.
units.rightText: When they had gathered at Mizpah, they drew water and poured it out before the LORD. On that day they fasted, and there they confessed, “We have sinned against the LORD.” And Samuel judged the Israelites at Mizpah.
rightNotes: 7:6 Or governed or led; similarly in verses 15, 16, and 17

units.leftText: When the Philistines heard that the children of Israel were gathered together at Mizpah, the lords of the Philistines went up against Israel. When the children of Israel heard it, they were afraid of the Philistines.
units.rightText: When the Philistines heard that the Israelites had gathered at Mizpah, their rulers marched up toward Israel. And when the Israelites learned of this, they feared the Philistines

units.leftText: The children of Israel said to Samuel, “Don’t stop crying to the LORD our God for us, that he will save us out of the hand of the Philistines.”
units.rightText: and said to Samuel, “Do not stop crying out to the LORD our God for us, that He may save us from the hand of the Philistines.”

units.leftText: Samuel took a suckling lamb, and offered it for a whole burnt offering to the LORD. Samuel cried to the LORD for Israel, and the LORD answered him.
units.rightText: Then Samuel took a suckling lamb and offered it as a whole burnt offering to the LORD. He cried out to the LORD on behalf of Israel, and the LORD answered him.

units.leftText: As Samuel was offering up the burnt offering, the Philistines came near to battle against Israel; but the LORD thundered with a great thunder on that day on the Philistines and confused them; and they were struck down before Israel.
units.rightText: As the Philistines drew near to fight against Israel, Samuel was offering up the burnt offering. But that day the LORD thundered loudly against the Philistines and threw them into such confusion that they fled before Israel.

units.leftText: The men of Israel went out of Mizpah and pursued the Philistines, and struck them until they came under Beth Kar.
units.rightText: Then the men of Israel charged out of Mizpah and pursued the Philistines, striking them down all the way to an area below Beth-car.

units.leftText: Then Samuel took a stone and set it between Mizpah and Shen, and called its name Ebenezer, saying, “The LORD helped us until now.”
units.rightText: Afterward, Samuel took a stone and set it up between Mizpah and Shen. He named it Ebenezer, saying, “Thus far the LORD has helped us.”
leftNotes: 7:12 “Ebenezer” means “stone of help”.
rightNotes: 7:12 Hebrew; LXX and Syriac Jeshanah
7:12 Ebenezer means stone of help.

units.leftText: So the Philistines were subdued, and they stopped coming within the border of Israel. The LORD’s hand was against the Philistines all the days of Samuel.
units.rightText: So the Philistines were subdued, and they stopped invading the territory of Israel. And the hand of the LORD was against the Philistines all the days of Samuel.

units.leftText: The cities which the Philistines had taken from Israel were restored to Israel, from Ekron even to Gath; and Israel recovered its border out of the hand of the Philistines. There was peace between Israel and the Amorites.
units.rightText: The cities from Ekron to Gath, which the Philistines had taken, were restored to Israel, who also delivered the surrounding territory from the hand of the Philistines. And there was peace between the Israelites and the Amorites.

units.leftText: Samuel judged Israel all the days of his life.
units.rightText: So Samuel judged Israel all the days of his life.

units.leftText: He went from year to year in a circuit to Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah; and he judged Israel in all those places.
units.rightText: Every year he would go on a circuit from Bethel to Gilgal to Mizpah, judging Israel in all these places.

units.leftText: His return was to Ramah, for his house was there, and he judged Israel there; and he built an altar to the LORD there.
units.rightText: Then he would return to Ramah because his home was there, and there he judged Israel and built an altar to the LORD.

units.leftText: When Samuel was old, he made his sons judges over Israel.
units.rightText: When Samuel grew old, he appointed his sons as judges over Israel.
rightNotes: 8:1 Or governors or leaders; similarly in verses 2, 5, 6, and 20

units.leftText: Now the name of his firstborn was Joel, and the name of his second, Abijah. They were judges in Beersheba.
units.rightText: The name of his firstborn son was Joel, and the name of his second was Abijah. They were judges in Beersheba.

units.leftText: His sons didn’t walk in his ways, but turned away after dishonest gain, took bribes, and perverted justice.
units.rightText: But his sons did not walk in his ways; they turned aside toward dishonest gain, accepting bribes and perverting justice.

units.leftText: Then all the elders of Israel gathered themselves together and came to Samuel to Ramah.
units.rightText: So all the elders of Israel gathered together and came to Samuel at Ramah.

units.leftText: They said to him, “Behold, you are old, and your sons don’t walk in your ways. Now make us a king to judge us like all the nations.”
units.rightText: “Look,” they said, “you are old, and your sons do not walk in your ways. Now appoint a king to judge us like all the other nations.”

units.leftText: But the thing displeased Samuel when they said, “Give us a king to judge us.”
units.rightText: But when they said, “Give us a king to judge us,” their demand was displeasing in the sight of Samuel; so he prayed to the LORD.

units.leftText: The LORD said to Samuel, “Listen to the voice of the people in all that they tell you; for they have not rejected you, but they have rejected me as the king over them.
units.rightText: And the LORD said to Samuel, “Listen to the voice of the people in all that they say to you. For it is not you they have rejected, but they have rejected Me as their king.

units.leftText: According to all the works which they have done since the day that I brought them up out of Egypt even to this day, in that they have forsaken me and served other gods, so they also do to you.
units.rightText: Just as they have done from the day I brought them up out of Egypt until this day, forsaking Me and serving other gods, so they are doing to you.

units.leftText: Now therefore, listen to their voice. However, you shall protest solemnly to them, and shall show them the way of the king who will reign over them.”
units.rightText: Now listen to their voice; but you must solemnly warn them and show them the manner of the king who will reign over them.”

units.leftText: Samuel told all the LORD’s words to the people who asked him for a king.
units.rightText: So Samuel spoke all the words of the LORD to the people who were asking him for a king.

units.leftText: He said, “This will be the way of the king who shall reign over you: he will take your sons and appoint them as his servants, for his chariots and to be his horsemen; and they will run before his chariots.
units.rightText: He said, “This will be the manner of the king who will reign over you: He will take your sons and appoint them to serve his own chariots and horses, and to run in front of his chariots.

units.leftText: He will appoint them to him for captains of thousands and captains of fifties; and he will assign some to plow his ground and to reap his harvest; and to make his instruments of war and the instruments of his chariots.
units.rightText: He will appoint some for himself as commanders of thousands and of fifties, and others to plow his ground, to reap his harvest, and to make his weapons of war and equipment for his chariots.

units.leftText: He will take your daughters to be perfumers, to be cooks, and to be bakers.
units.rightText: And he will take your daughters to be perfumers, cooks, and bakers.

units.leftText: He will take your fields, your vineyards, and your olive groves, even your best, and give them to his servants.
units.rightText: He will take the best of your fields and vineyards and olive groves and give them to his servants.

units.leftText: He will take one tenth of your seed and of your vineyards, and give it to his officers and to his servants.
units.rightText: He will take a tenth of your grain and grape harvest and give it to his officials and servants.

units.leftText: He will take your male servants, your female servants, your best young men, and your donkeys, and assign them to his own work.
units.rightText: And he will take your menservants and maidservants and your best cattle and donkeys and put them to his own use.
rightNotes: 8:16 LXX; Hebrew your best young men

units.leftText: He will take one tenth of your flocks; and you will be his servants.
units.rightText: He will take a tenth of your flocks, and you yourselves will become his slaves.

units.leftText: You will cry out in that day because of your king whom you will have chosen for yourselves; and the LORD will not answer you in that day.”
units.rightText: When that day comes, you will beg for relief from the king you have chosen, but the LORD will not answer you on that day.”

units.leftText: But the people refused to listen to the voice of Samuel; and they said, “No, but we will have a king over us,
units.rightText: Nevertheless , the people refused to listen to Samuel. “No!” they said. “We must have a king over us.

units.leftText: that we also may be like all the nations; and that our king may judge us, and go out before us, and fight our battles.”
units.rightText: Then we will be like all the other nations, with a king to judge us, to go out before us, and to fight our battles.”

units.leftText: Samuel heard all the words of the people, and he rehearsed them in the ears of the LORD.
units.rightText: Samuel listened to all the words of the people and repeated them in the hearing of the LORD.

units.leftText: The LORD said to Samuel, “Listen to their voice, and make them a king.”
units.rightText: “Listen to their voice,” the LORD said to Samuel. “Appoint a king for them.”

units.leftText: Now there was a man of Benjamin, whose name was Kish the son of Abiel, the son of Zeror, the son of Becorath, the son of Aphiah, the son of a Benjamite, a mighty man of valor.
units.rightText: Now there was a Benjamite, a powerful man, whose name was Kish son of Abiel, the son of Zeror, the son of Becorath, the son of Aphiah of Benjamin.

units.leftText: He had a son whose name was Saul, an impressive young man; and there was not among the children of Israel a more handsome person than he. From his shoulders and upward he was taller than any of the people.
units.rightText: And he had a son named Saul, choice and handsome, without equal among the Israelites — a head taller than any of the people.

units.leftText: The donkeys of Kish, Saul’s father, were lost. Kish said to Saul his son, “Now take one of the servants with you, and arise, go look for the donkeys.”
units.rightText: One day the donkeys of Saul’s father Kish wandered off, and Kish said to his son Saul, “Take one of the servants and go look for the donkeys.”

units.leftText: He passed through the hill country of Ephraim, and passed through the land of Shalishah, but they didn’t find them. Then they passed through the land of Shaalim, and they weren’t there. Then he passed through the land of the Benjamites, but they didn’t find them.
units.rightText: So Saul passed through the hill country of Ephraim and then through the land of Shalishah, but they did not find the donkeys. He and the servant went through the region of Shaalim, but they were not there. Then they went through the land of Benjamin, and still they did not find them.

units.leftText: When they had come to the land of Zuph, Saul said to his servant who was with him, “Come! Let’s return, lest my father stop caring about the donkeys and be anxious for us.”
units.rightText: When they reached the land of Zuph, Saul said to his servant, “Come, let us go back, or my father will stop worrying about the donkeys and start worrying about us.”

units.leftText: The servant said to him, “Behold now, there is a man of God in this city, and he is a man who is held in honor. All that he says surely happens. Now let’s go there. Perhaps he can tell us which way to go.”
units.rightText: “Look,” said the servant, “in this city there is a man of God who is highly respected; everything he says surely comes to pass. Let us go there now. Perhaps he will tell us which way to go.”

units.leftText: Then Saul said to his servant, “But behold, if we go, what should we bring the man? For the bread is spent in our sacks, and there is not a present to bring to the man of God. What do we have?”
units.rightText: “If we do go,” Saul replied, “what can we give the man? For the bread in our packs is gone, and there is no gift to take to the man of God. What do we have?”

units.leftText: The servant answered Saul again and said, “Behold, I have in my hand the fourth part of a shekel of silver. I will give that to the man of God, to tell us our way.”
units.rightText: The servant answered him again. “Look,” he said, “I have here in my hand a quarter shekel of silver. I will give it to the man of God, and he will tell us our way.”
leftNotes: 9:8 A shekel is about 10 grams or about 0.35 ounces, so 1/4 shekel would be a small coin of about 2.5 grams.
rightNotes: 9:8 A quarter shekel is approximately 0.1 ounces or 2.85 grams of silver.

units.leftText: (In earlier times in Israel, when a man went to inquire of God, he said, “Come! Let’s go to the seer;” for he who is now called a prophet was before called a seer.)
units.rightText: (Formerly in Israel, a man on his way to inquire of God would say, “Come, let us go to the seer.” For the prophet of today was formerly called the seer.)

units.leftText: Then Saul said to his servant, “Well said. Come! Let’s go.” So they went to the city where the man of God was.
units.rightText: “Good,” said Saul to his servant. “Come, let us go.” So they set out for the city where the man of God was.

units.leftText: As they went up the ascent to the city, they found young maidens going out to draw water, and said to them, “Is the seer here?”
units.rightText: And as they were climbing the hill to the city, they met some young women coming out to draw water and asked, “Is the seer here?”

units.leftText: They answered them and said, “He is. Behold, he is before you. Hurry now, for he has come today into the city; for the people have a sacrifice today in the high place.
units.rightText: “Yes, he is ahead of you,” they answered. “Hurry now, for today he has come to the city because the people have a sacrifice on the high place.

units.leftText: As soon as you have come into the city, you will immediately find him before he goes up to the high place to eat; for the people will not eat until he comes, because he blesses the sacrifice. Afterwards those who are invited eat. Now therefore go up; for at this time you will find him.”
units.rightText: As soon as you enter the city, you will find him before he goes up to the high place to eat. The people will not eat until he comes, because he must bless the sacrifice; after that, the guests will eat. Go up at once; you will find him.”

units.leftText: They went up to the city. As they came within the city, behold, Samuel came out toward them to go up to the high place.
units.rightText: So Saul and his servant went up toward the city, and as they were entering it, there was Samuel coming toward them on his way up to the high place.

units.leftText: Now the LORD had revealed to Samuel a day before Saul came, saying,
units.rightText: Now on the day before Saul’s arrival, the LORD had revealed to Samuel,

units.leftText: “Tomorrow about this time I will send you a man out of the land of Benjamin, and you shall anoint him to be prince over my people Israel. He will save my people out of the hand of the Philistines; for I have looked upon my people, because their cry has come to me.”
units.rightText: “At this time tomorrow I will send you a man from the land of Benjamin, and you are to anoint him ruler over My people Israel; he will save them from the hand of the Philistines. For I have looked upon My people, because their cry has come to Me.”

units.leftText: When Samuel saw Saul, the LORD said to him, “Behold, the man of whom I spoke to you! He will have authority over my people.”
units.rightText: When Samuel saw Saul, the LORD told him, “Here is the man of whom I spoke; he shall rule over My people.”

units.leftText: Then Saul approached Samuel in the gateway, and said, “Please tell me where the seer’s house is.”
units.rightText: Saul approached Samuel in the gateway and asked, “Would you please tell me where the seer’s house is?”

units.leftText: Samuel answered Saul and said, “I am the seer. Go up before me to the high place, for you are to eat with me today. In the morning I will let you go and will tell you all that is in your heart.
units.rightText: “I am the seer,” Samuel replied. “Go up before me to the high place, for you shall eat with me today. And when I send you off in the morning, I will tell you all that is in your heart.

units.leftText: As for your donkeys who were lost three days ago, don’t set your mind on them, for they have been found. For whom does all Israel desire? Is it not you and all your father’s house?”
units.rightText: As for the donkeys you lost three days ago, do not worry about them, for they have been found. And upon whom is all the desire of Israel, if not upon you and all your father’s house?”

units.leftText: Saul answered, “Am I not a Benjamite, of the smallest of the tribes of Israel? And my family the least of all the families of the tribe of Benjamin? Why then do you speak to me like this?”
units.rightText: Saul replied, “Am I not a Benjamite from the smallest tribe of Israel, and is not my clan the least of all the clans of Benjamin? So why would you say such a thing to me?”

units.leftText: Samuel took Saul and his servant and brought them into the guest room, and made them sit in the best place among those who were invited, who were about thirty persons.
units.rightText: Then Samuel took Saul and his servant, brought them into the hall, and seated them in the place of honor among those who were invited — about thirty in all.

units.leftText: Samuel said to the cook, “Bring the portion which I gave you, of which I said to you, ‘Set it aside.’”
units.rightText: And Samuel said to the cook, “Bring the portion I gave you and told you to set aside.”

units.leftText: The cook took up the thigh, and that which was on it, and set it before Saul. Samuel said, “Behold, that which has been reserved! Set it before yourself and eat; because it has been kept for you for the appointed time, for I said, ‘I have invited the people.’” So Saul ate with Samuel that day.
units.rightText: So the cook picked up the leg and what was attached to it and set it before Saul. Then Samuel said, “Here is what was kept back. It was set apart for you. Eat, for it has been kept for you for this occasion, from the time I said, ‘I have invited the people.’” So Saul dined with Samuel that day.

units.leftText: When they had come down from the high place into the city, he talked with Saul on the housetop.
units.rightText: And after they had come down from the high place into the city, Samuel spoke with Saul on the roof of his house.

units.leftText: They arose early; and about daybreak, Samuel called to Saul on the housetop, saying, “Get up, that I may send you away.” Saul arose, and they both went outside, he and Samuel, together.
units.rightText: They got up early in the morning, and just before dawn Samuel called to Saul on the roof, “Get ready, and I will send you on your way!” So Saul got ready, and both he and Samuel went outside together.

units.leftText: As they were going down at the end of the city, Samuel said to Saul, “Tell the servant to go on ahead of us.” He went ahead, then Samuel said, “But stand still first, that I may cause you to hear God’s message.”
units.rightText: As they were going down to the edge of the city, Samuel said to Saul, “Tell the servant to go on ahead of us, but you stay for a while, and I will reveal to you the word of God.” So the servant went on.

units.leftText: Then Samuel took the vial of oil and poured it on his head, then kissed him and said, “Hasn’t the LORD anointed you to be prince over his inheritance?
units.rightText: Then Samuel took a flask of oil, poured it on Saul’s head, kissed him, and said, “Has not the LORD anointed you ruler over His inheritance?
rightNotes: 10:1 Hebrew; LXX “Has not the LORD anointed you ruler over Israel? And you will rule over the LORD’s people and save them from their enemies around them. This will be the sign to you that the LORD has appointed you to be leader over His inheritance.

units.leftText: When you have departed from me today, then you will find two men by Rachel’s tomb, on the border of Benjamin at Zelzah. They will tell you, ‘The donkeys which you went to look for have been found; and behold, your father has stopped caring about the donkeys and is anxious for you, saying, “What shall I do for my son?”’
units.rightText: When you leave me today, you will find two men at Rachel’s tomb in Zelzah on the border of Benjamin. They will say to you, ‘The donkeys you seek have been found, and now your father has stopped worrying about the donkeys and started worrying about you, asking, “What should I do about my son?”’

units.leftText: “Then you will go on forward from there, and you will come to the oak of Tabor. Three men will meet you there going up to God to Bethel: one carrying three young goats, and another carrying three loaves of bread, and another carrying a container of wine.
units.rightText: Then you will go on from there until you come to the Oak of Tabor. Three men going up to God at Bethel will meet you there, one carrying three young goats, another carrying three loaves of bread, and another carrying a skin of wine.
rightNotes: 10:3 Or Terebinth or Great Tree

units.leftText: They will greet you and give you two loaves of bread, which you shall receive from their hand.
units.rightText: They will greet you and give you two loaves of bread, which you will accept from their hands.

units.leftText: “After that you will come to the hill of God, where the garrison of the Philistines is; and it will happen, when you have come there to the city, that you will meet a band of prophets coming down from the high place with a lute, a tambourine, a pipe, and a harp before them; and they will be prophesying.
units.rightText: After that you will come to Gibeah of God, where the Philistines have an outpost. As you approach the city, you will meet a group of prophets coming down from the high place, preceded by harps, tambourines, flutes, and lyres, and they will be prophesying.
rightNotes: 10:5 Hebrew Gibeath-Elohim, meaning the hill of God

units.leftText: Then the LORD’s Spirit will come mightily on you, then you will prophesy with them and will be turned into another man.
units.rightText: Then the Spirit of the LORD will rush upon you, and you will prophesy with them; and you will be transformed into a different person.

units.leftText: Let it be, when these signs have come to you, that you do what is appropriate for the occasion; for God is with you.
units.rightText: When these signs have come, do as the occasion demands, for God is with you.

units.leftText: “Go down ahead of me to Gilgal; and behold, I will come down to you to offer burnt offerings and to sacrifice sacrifices of peace offerings. Wait seven days, until I come to you and show you what you are to do.”
units.rightText: And you shall go before me to Gilgal, and surely I will come to you to offer burnt offerings and to sacrifice peace offerings. Wait seven days until I come to you and show you what you are to do.”

units.leftText: It was so, that when he had turned his back to go from Samuel, God gave him another heart; and all those signs happened that day.
units.rightText: As Saul turned to leave Samuel, God changed Saul’s heart, and all the signs came to pass that day.

units.leftText: When they came there to the hill, behold, a band of prophets met him; and the Spirit of God came mightily on him, and he prophesied among them.
units.rightText: When Saul and his servant arrived at Gibeah, a group of prophets met him. Then the Spirit of God rushed upon him, and he prophesied along with them.
rightNotes: 10:10 Gibeah means the hill.

units.leftText: When all who knew him before saw that, behold, he prophesied with the prophets, then the people said to one another, “What is this that has come to the son of Kish? Is Saul also among the prophets?”
units.rightText: When all those who had formerly known Saul saw him prophesying with the prophets, they asked one another, “What has happened to the son of Kish? Is Saul also among the prophets?”

units.leftText: One from the same place answered, “Who is their father?” Therefore it became a proverb, “Is Saul also among the prophets?”
units.rightText: Then a man who lived there replied, “And who is their father?” So the saying became a proverb: “Is Saul also among the prophets?”

units.leftText: When he had finished prophesying, he came to the high place.
units.rightText: And when Saul had finished prophesying, he went up to the high place.

units.leftText: Saul’s uncle said to him and to his servant, “Where did you go?”
units.rightText: Now Saul’s uncle asked him and his servant, “Where did you go?”

units.leftText: Saul’s uncle said, “Please tell me what Samuel said to you.”
units.rightText: “Tell me,” Saul’s uncle asked, “what did Samuel say to you?”

units.leftText: Saul said to his uncle, “He told us plainly that the donkeys were found.” But concerning the matter of the kingdom, of which Samuel spoke, he didn’t tell him.
units.rightText: And Saul replied, “He assured us that the donkeys had been found.” But Saul did not tell his uncle what Samuel had said about the kingship.

units.leftText: Samuel called the people together to the LORD to Mizpah;
units.rightText: After this, Samuel summoned the people to the LORD at Mizpah

units.leftText: and he said to the children of Israel, “The LORD, the God of Israel, says ‘I brought Israel up out of Egypt and I delivered you out of the hand of the Egyptians, and out of the hand of all the kingdoms that oppressed you.’
units.rightText: and said to the Israelites, “This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: ‘I brought Israel up out of Egypt, and I rescued you from the hands of the Egyptians and of all the kingdoms that oppressed you.’

units.leftText: But you have today rejected your God, who himself saves you out of all your calamities and your distresses; and you have said to him, ‘No! Set a king over us!’ Now therefore present yourselves before the LORD by your tribes and by your thousands.”
units.rightText: But today you have rejected your God, who saves you from all your troubles and afflictions, and you have said to Him, ‘No, set a king over us.’ Now therefore present yourselves before the LORD by your tribes and clans.”

units.leftText: So Samuel brought all the tribes of Israel near, and the tribe of Benjamin was chosen.
units.rightText: Thus Samuel had all the tribes of Israel come forward, and the tribe of Benjamin was selected.

units.leftText: He brought the tribe of Benjamin near by their families and the family of the Matrites was chosen. Then Saul the son of Kish was chosen; but when they looked for him, he could not be found.
units.rightText: Then he had the tribe of Benjamin come forward by its clans, and the clan of Matri was selected. Finally, Saul son of Kish was selected. But when they looked for him, they could not find him.
rightNotes: 10:21 LXX includes And he brought the family of the Matrites near, man by man.

units.leftText: Therefore they asked of the LORD further, “Is there yet a man to come here?”
units.rightText: So again they inquired of the LORD, “Has the man come here yet?”

units.leftText: They ran and got him there. When he stood among the people, he was higher than any of the people from his shoulders and upward.
units.rightText: So they ran and brought Saul, and when he stood among the people, he was a head taller than any of the others.

units.leftText: Samuel said to all the people, “Do you see him whom the LORD has chosen, that there is no one like him among all the people?”
units.rightText: Samuel said to all the people, “Do you see the one the LORD has chosen? There is no one like him among all the people.”

units.leftText: Then Samuel told the people the regulations of the kingdom, and wrote it in a book and laid it up before the LORD. Samuel sent all the people away, every man to his house.
units.rightText: Then Samuel explained to the people the rights of kingship. He wrote them on a scroll and laid it up before the LORD. And Samuel sent all the people away, each to his own home.

units.leftText: Saul also went to his house in Gibeah; and the army went with him, whose hearts God had touched.
units.rightText: Saul also went to his home in Gibeah, and the men of valor whose hearts God had touched went with him.

units.leftText: But certain worthless fellows said, “How could this man save us?” They despised him, and brought him no tribute. But he held his peace.
units.rightText: But some worthless men said, “How can this man save us?” So they despised him and brought him no gifts; but Saul remained silent about it.
rightNotes: 10:27 MT and LXX; one DSS manuscript includes Nahash, king of the Ammonites, had viciously oppressed the people of Gad and Reuben, gouging out the right eye of each Israelite dwelling there. He would not allow anyone to rescue them, and there was no Israelite east of the Jordan whose right eye had not been gouged out. But 7,000 men had escaped from the Ammonites and settled in Jabesh-gilead.

units.leftText: Then Nahash the Ammonite came up and encamped against Jabesh Gilead; and all the men of Jabesh said to Nahash, “Make a covenant with us, and we will serve you.”
units.rightText: Then Nahash the Ammonite came up and laid siege to Jabesh-gilead. All the men of Jabesh said to him, “Make a treaty with us, and we will serve you.”
rightNotes: 11:1 DSS and LXX About a month later Nahash
11:1 Forms of the Hebrew berit are translated in most passages as covenant.

units.leftText: Nahash the Ammonite said to them, “On this condition I will make it with you, that all your right eyes be gouged out. I will make this dishonor all Israel.”
units.rightText: But Nahash the Ammonite replied, “I will make a treaty with you on one condition, that I may put out everyone’s right eye and bring reproach upon all Israel.”

units.leftText: The elders of Jabesh said to him, “Give us seven days, that we may send messengers to all the borders of Israel; and then, if there is no one to save us, we will come out to you.”
units.rightText: “Hold off for seven days,” replied the elders of Jabesh, “and let us send messengers throughout Israel. If there is no one to save us, we will surrender to you.”

units.leftText: Then the messengers came to Gibeah of Saul, and spoke these words in the ears of the people, then all the people lifted up their voice and wept.
units.rightText: When the messengers came to Gibeah of Saul and relayed these words in the hearing of the people, they all wept aloud.

units.leftText: Behold, Saul came following the oxen out of the field; and Saul said, “What ails the people that they weep?” They told him the words of the men of Jabesh.
units.rightText: Just then Saul was returning from the field, behind his oxen. “What troubles the people?” asked Saul. “Why are they weeping?” And they relayed to him the words of the men from Jabesh.

units.leftText: God’s Spirit came mightily on Saul when he heard those words, and his anger burned hot.
units.rightText: When Saul heard their words, the Spirit of God rushed upon him, and he burned with great anger.

units.leftText: He took a yoke of oxen and cut them in pieces, then sent them throughout all the borders of Israel by the hand of messengers, saying, “Whoever doesn’t come out after Saul and after Samuel, so shall it be done to his oxen.” The dread of the LORD fell on the people, and they came out as one man.
units.rightText: He took a pair of oxen, cut them into pieces, and sent them by messengers throughout the land of Israel, proclaiming, “This is what will be done to the oxen of anyone who does not march behind Saul and Samuel.”

units.leftText: He counted them in Bezek; and the children of Israel were three hundred thousand, and the men of Judah thirty thousand.
units.rightText: And when Saul numbered them at Bezek, there were 300,000 Israelites and 30,000 men of Judah.
rightNotes: 11:8 DSS and LXX 70,000

units.leftText: They said to the messengers who came, “Tell the men of Jabesh Gilead, ‘Tomorrow, by the time the sun is hot, you will be rescued.’” The messengers came and told the men of Jabesh; and they were glad.
units.rightText: So they said to the messengers who had come, “Tell the men of Jabesh-gilead: ‘Deliverance will be yours tomorrow by the time the sun is hot.’”

units.leftText: Therefore the men of Jabesh said, “Tomorrow we will come out to you, and you shall do with us all that seems good to you.”
units.rightText: Then the men of Jabesh said to Nahash, “Tomorrow we will come out, and you can do with us whatever seems good to you.”

units.leftText: On the next day, Saul put the people in three companies; and they came into the middle of the camp in the morning watch, and struck the Ammonites until the heat of the day. Those who remained were scattered, so that no two of them were left together.
units.rightText: The next day Saul organized the troops into three divisions, and during the morning watch they invaded the camp of the Ammonites and slaughtered them, until the hottest part of the day. And the survivors were so scattered that no two of them were left together.
