units.leftText: The people said to Samuel, “Who is he who said, ‘Shall Saul reign over us?’ Bring those men, that we may put them to death!”
units.rightText: Then the people said to Samuel, “Who said that Saul should not reign over us? Bring those men here so we can kill them!”

units.leftText: Saul said, “No man shall be put to death today; for today the LORD has rescued Israel.”
units.rightText: But Saul ordered, “No one shall be put to death this day, for today the LORD has worked salvation in Israel.”

units.leftText: Then Samuel said to the people, “Come! Let’s go to Gilgal, and renew the kingdom there.”
units.rightText: Then Samuel said to the people, “Come, let us go to Gilgal and renew the kingship there.”

units.leftText: All the people went to Gilgal; and there they made Saul king before the LORD in Gilgal. There they offered sacrifices of peace offerings before the LORD; and there Saul and all the men of Israel rejoiced greatly.
units.rightText: So all the people went to Gilgal and confirmed Saul as king in the presence of the LORD. There they sacrificed peace offerings before the LORD, and Saul and all the Israelites rejoiced greatly.

units.leftText: Samuel said to all Israel, “Behold, I have listened to your voice in all that you said to me, and have made a king over you.
units.rightText: Then Samuel said to all Israel, “I have listened to your voice in all that you have said to me, and I have set over you a king.

units.leftText: Now, behold, the king walks before you. I am old and gray-headed. Behold, my sons are with you. I have walked before you from my youth to this day.
units.rightText: Now here is the king walking before you, and I am old and gray, and my sons are here with you. I have walked before you from my youth until this day.

units.leftText: Here I am. Witness against me before the LORD and before his anointed. Whose ox have I taken? Whose donkey have I taken? Whom have I defrauded? Whom have I oppressed? Of whose hand have I taken a bribe to make me blind my eyes? I will restore it to you.”
units.rightText: Here I am. Bear witness against me before the LORD and before His anointed: Whose ox or donkey have I taken? Whom have I cheated or oppressed? From whose hand have I accepted a bribe and closed my eyes? Tell me, and I will restore it to you.”
rightNotes: 12:3 Hebrew And I will restore it; LXX Testify against me, and I will restore it

units.leftText: They said, “You have not defrauded us, nor oppressed us, neither have you taken anything from anyone’s hand.”
units.rightText: “You have not cheated us or oppressed us,” they replied, “nor have you taken anything from the hand of man.”

units.leftText: He said to them, “The LORD is witness against you, and his anointed is witness today, that you have not found anything in my hand.”
units.rightText: Samuel said to them, “The LORD is a witness against you, and His anointed is a witness today, that you have not found anything in my hand.”

units.leftText: Samuel said to the people, “It is the LORD who appointed Moses and Aaron, and that brought your fathers up out of the land of Egypt.
units.rightText: Then Samuel said to the people, “The LORD is the One who appointed Moses and Aaron, and who brought your fathers up out of the land of Egypt.
rightNotes: 12:6 Hebrew; LXX The LORD is the witness who

units.leftText: Now therefore stand still, that I may plead with you before the LORD concerning all the righteous acts of the LORD, which he did to you and to your fathers.
units.rightText: Now present yourselves, so that I may confront you before the LORD with all the righteous acts He has done for you and your fathers.

units.leftText: “When Jacob had come into Egypt, and your fathers cried to the LORD, then the LORD sent Moses and Aaron, who brought your fathers out of Egypt, and made them to dwell in this place.
units.rightText: When Jacob went to Egypt, your fathers cried out to the LORD, and He sent them Moses and Aaron, who brought your fathers out of Egypt and settled them in this place.
rightNotes: 12:8 Hebrew; LXX includes and the Egyptians oppressed them

units.leftText: But they forgot the LORD their God; and he sold them into the hand of Sisera, captain of the army of Hazor, and into the hand of the Philistines, and into the hand of the king of Moab; and they fought against them.
units.rightText: But they forgot the LORD their God, and He sold them into the hand of Sisera the commander of the army of Hazor, and into the hands of the Philistines and the king of Moab, who fought against them.
rightNotes: 12:9 LXX the army of Jabin king of Hazor

units.leftText: They cried to the LORD, and said, ‘We have sinned, because we have forsaken the LORD and have served the Baals and the Ashtaroth; but now deliver us out of the hand of our enemies, and we will serve you.’
units.rightText: Then they cried out to the LORD and said, ‘We have sinned, for we have forsaken the LORD and served the Baals and Ashtoreths. Now deliver us from the hands of our enemies, that we may serve You.’

units.leftText: The LORD sent Jerubbaal, Bedan, Jephthah, and Samuel, and delivered you out of the hand of your enemies on every side; and you lived in safety.
units.rightText: So the LORD sent Jerubbaal, Barak, Jephthah, and Samuel, and He delivered you from the hands of your enemies on every side, and you dwelt securely.
rightNotes: 12:11 Jerubbaal is another name for Gideon and probably means let Baal contend; see Judges 6:32|JDG 6:32*.
12:11 LXX and Syriac; Hebrew Bedan
12:11 LXX and Syriac Samson

units.leftText: “When you saw that Nahash the king of the children of Ammon came against you, you said to me, ‘No, but a king shall reign over us,’ when the LORD your God was your king.
units.rightText: But when you saw that Nahash king of the Ammonites was moving against you, you said to me, ‘No, we must have a king to rule over us’— even though the LORD your God was your king.

units.leftText: Now therefore see the king whom you have chosen and whom you have asked for. Behold, the LORD has set a king over you.
units.rightText: Now here is the king you have chosen, the one you requested. Behold, the LORD has placed a king over you.

units.leftText: If you will fear the LORD, and serve him, and listen to his voice, and not rebel against the commandment of the LORD, then both you and also the king who reigns over you are followers of the LORD your God.
units.rightText: If you fear the LORD and serve Him and obey His voice, and if you do not rebel against the command of the LORD, and if both you and the king who rules over you follow the LORD your God, then all will be well.
rightNotes: 12:14 then all will be well is implied; Literally If you fear the LORD and serve Him and obey His voice, and if you do not rebel against the command of the LORD, (then) both you and the king who reigns over you will follow the LORD your God.

units.leftText: But if you will not listen to the LORD’s voice, but rebel against the commandment of the LORD, then the LORD’s hand will be against you, as it was against your fathers.
units.rightText: But if you disobey the LORD and rebel against His command, then the hand of the LORD will be against you as it was against your fathers.
rightNotes: 12:15 Hebrew; LXX against your king

units.leftText: “Now therefore stand still and see this great thing, which the LORD will do before your eyes.
units.rightText: Now, therefore, present yourselves and see this great thing that the LORD will do before your eyes.

units.leftText: Isn’t it wheat harvest today? I will call to the LORD, that he may send thunder and rain; and you will know and see that your wickedness is great, which you have done in the LORD’s sight, in asking for a king.”
units.rightText: Is it not the wheat harvest today? I will call on the LORD to send thunder and rain, so that you will know and see what a great evil you have committed in the sight of the LORD by asking for a king.”

units.leftText: So Samuel called to the LORD, and the LORD sent thunder and rain that day. Then all the people greatly feared the LORD and Samuel.
units.rightText: So Samuel called to the LORD, and on that day the LORD sent thunder and rain.

units.leftText: All the people said to Samuel, “Pray for your servants to the LORD your God, that we not die; for we have added to all our sins this evil, to ask for a king.”
units.rightText: They pleaded with Samuel, “Pray to the LORD your God for your servants so that we will not die! For we have added to all our sins the evil of asking for a king.”

units.leftText: Samuel said to the people, “Don’t be afraid. You have indeed done all this evil; yet don’t turn away from following the LORD, but serve the LORD with all your heart.
units.rightText: “Do not be afraid,” Samuel replied. “Even though you have committed all this evil, do not turn aside from following the LORD, but serve the LORD with all your heart.

units.leftText: Don’t turn away to go after vain things which can’t profit or deliver, for they are vain.
units.rightText: Do not turn aside after worthless things that cannot profit you or deliver you, for they are empty.

units.leftText: For the LORD will not forsake his people for his great name’s sake, because it has pleased the LORD to make you a people for himself.
units.rightText: Indeed, for the sake of His great name, the LORD will not abandon His people, because He was pleased to make you His own.

units.leftText: Moreover, as for me, far be it from me that I should sin against the LORD in ceasing to pray for you; but I will instruct you in the good and the right way.
units.rightText: As for me, far be it from me that I should sin against the LORD by ceasing to pray for you. And I will continue to teach you the good and right way.

units.leftText: Only fear the LORD, and serve him in truth with all your heart; for consider what great things he has done for you.
units.rightText: Above all, fear the LORD and serve Him faithfully with all your heart; consider what great things He has done for you.

units.leftText: But if you keep doing evil, you will be consumed, both you and your king.”
units.rightText: But if you persist in doing evil, both you and your king will be swept away.”

units.leftText: Saul was thirty years old when he became king, and he reigned over Israel forty-two years.
units.rightText: Saul was thirty years old when he became king, and he reigned over Israel forty-two years.
leftNotes: 13:1 The traditional Hebrew text omits “thirty” and “forty-”. The blanks are filled in here from a few manuscripts of the Septuagint.
rightNotes: 13:1 A few late LXX manuscripts; MT Saul was a son of a year
13:1 Or over Israel forty years(see Acts 13:21|ACT 13:21*); MT over Israel two years

units.leftText: Saul chose for himself three thousand men of Israel, of which two thousand were with Saul in Michmash and in the Mount of Bethel, and one thousand were with Jonathan in Gibeah of Benjamin. He sent the rest of the people to their own tents.
units.rightText: He chose for himself three thousand men of Israel: Two thousand were with Saul at Michmash and in the hill country of Bethel, and a thousand were with Jonathan in Gibeah of Benjamin. And the rest of the troops he sent away, each to his own home.

units.leftText: Jonathan struck the garrison of the Philistines that was in Geba, and the Philistines heard of it. Saul blew the trumpet throughout all the land, saying, “Let the Hebrews hear!”
units.rightText: Then Jonathan attacked the Philistine outpost at Geba, and the Philistines heard about it. So Saul blew the ram’s horn throughout the land, saying, “Let the Hebrews hear!”

units.leftText: All Israel heard that Saul had struck the garrison of the Philistines, and also that Israel was considered an abomination to the Philistines. The people were gathered together after Saul to Gilgal.
units.rightText: And all Israel heard the news: “Saul has attacked an outpost of the Philistines, and now Israel has become a stench to the Philistines!” Then the people were summoned to join Saul at Gilgal.

units.leftText: The Philistines assembled themselves together to fight with Israel: thirty thousand chariots, six thousand horsemen, and people as the sand which is on the seashore in multitude. They came up and encamped in Michmash, eastward of Beth Aven.
units.rightText: Now the Philistines assembled to fight against Israel with three thousand chariots, six thousand horsemen, and troops as numerous as the sand on the seashore. They went up and camped at Michmash, east of Beth-aven.
rightNotes: 13:5 Some LXX manuscripts and Syriac; Hebrew thirty thousand

units.leftText: When the men of Israel saw that they were in trouble (for the people were distressed), then the people hid themselves in caves, in thickets, in rocks, in tombs, and in pits.
units.rightText: Seeing that they were in danger because their troops were hard-pressed, the men of Israel hid in caves and thickets, among the rocks, and in cellars and cisterns.

units.leftText: Now some of the Hebrews had gone over the Jordan to the land of Gad and Gilead; but as for Saul, he was yet in Gilgal, and all the people followed him trembling.
units.rightText: Some Hebrews even crossed the Jordan into the land of Gad and Gilead. Saul, however, remained at Gilgal, and all his troops were quaking in fear.

units.leftText: He stayed seven days, according to the time set by Samuel; but Samuel didn’t come to Gilgal, and the people were scattering from him.
units.rightText: And Saul waited seven days for the time appointed by Samuel, but Samuel did not come to Gilgal, and the troops began to desert Saul.

units.leftText: Saul said, “Bring the burnt offering to me here, and the peace offerings.” He offered the burnt offering.
units.rightText: So he said, “Bring me the burnt offering and the peace offerings.” And he offered up the burnt offering.

units.leftText: It came to pass that as soon as he had finished offering the burnt offering, behold, Samuel came; and Saul went out to meet him, that he might greet him.
units.rightText: Just as he finished offering the burnt offering, Samuel arrived, and Saul went out to greet him.

units.leftText: Samuel said, “What have you done?”
units.rightText: “What have you done?” Samuel asked.

units.leftText: therefore I said, ‘Now the Philistines will come down on me to Gilgal, and I haven’t entreated the favor of the LORD.’ I forced myself therefore, and offered the burnt offering.”
units.rightText: I thought, ‘Now the Philistines will descend upon me at Gilgal, and I have not sought the favor of the LORD.’ So I felt compelled to offer the burnt offering.”

units.leftText: Samuel said to Saul, “You have done foolishly. You have not kept the commandment of the LORD your God, which he commanded you; for now the LORD would have established your kingdom on Israel forever.
units.rightText: “You have acted foolishly,” Samuel declared. “You have not kept the command that the LORD your God gave you; if you had, the LORD would have established your kingdom over Israel for all time.

units.leftText: But now your kingdom will not continue. The LORD has sought for himself a man after his own heart, and the LORD has appointed him to be prince over his people, because you have not kept that which the LORD commanded you.”
units.rightText: But now your kingdom will not endure; the LORD has sought a man after His own heart and appointed him ruler over His people, because you have not kept the command of the LORD.”

units.leftText: Samuel arose, and went from Gilgal to Gibeah of Benjamin. Saul counted the people who were present with him, about six hundred men.
units.rightText: Then Samuel set out from Gilgal and went up to Gibeah in Benjamin. And Saul numbered the troops who were with him, about six hundred men.
rightNotes: 13:15 LXX Then Samuel set out, and the rest of the people went up after Saul to meet the army; they went up from Gilgal to Gibeah of Benjamin.

units.leftText: Saul, and Jonathan his son, and the people who were present with them, stayed in Geba of Benjamin; but the Philistines encamped in Michmash.
units.rightText: Now Saul and Jonathan his son and the troops with them were staying in Geba of Benjamin, while the Philistines camped at Michmash.

units.leftText: The raiders came out of the camp of the Philistines in three companies: one company turned to the way that leads to Ophrah, to the land of Shual;
units.rightText: And raiders went out of the Philistine camp in three divisions. One headed toward Ophrah in the land of Shual,

units.leftText: another company turned the way to Beth Horon; and another company turned the way of the border that looks down on the valley of Zeboim toward the wilderness.
units.rightText: another toward Beth-horon, and the third down the border road overlooking the Valley of Zeboim facing the wilderness.

units.leftText: Now there was no blacksmith found throughout all the land of Israel, for the Philistines said, “Lest the Hebrews make themselves swords or spears”;
units.rightText: And no blacksmith could be found in all the land of Israel, because the Philistines had said, “The Hebrews must not be allowed to make swords or spears.”

units.leftText: but all the Israelites went down to the Philistines, each man to sharpen his own plowshare, mattock, ax, and sickle.
units.rightText: Instead, all the Israelites would go down to the Philistines to sharpen their plowshares, mattocks, axes, and sickles.
rightNotes: 13:20 LXX; Hebrew and plowshares; (so plowshare appears twice in the Hebrew).

units.leftText: The price was one payim each to sharpen mattocks, plowshares, pitchforks, axes, and goads.
units.rightText: The charge was a pim for sharpening a plowshare or mattock, a third of a shekel for sharpening a pitchfork or an axe, and a third of a shekel for repointing an oxgoad.
leftNotes: 13:21 A payim (or pim) was 2/3 shekel of silver, or 0.26 ounces, or 7.6 grams
rightNotes: 13:21 A pim possibly refers to a polished stone weighing approximately 0.25 ounces or 7 grams found in excavations. This is equivalent to about two-thirds of a shekel and likely refers to the price charged by the Philistines for the services listed.
13:21 Hebrew does not include the currency unit of a shekel charged for sharpening a pitchfork, an axe, or an oxgoad; alternatively, possibly a third of a pim for each.

units.leftText: So it came to pass in the day of battle that neither sword nor spear was found in the hand of any of the people who were with Saul and Jonathan; but Saul and Jonathan his son had them.
units.rightText: So on the day of battle not a sword or spear could be found in the hands of the troops with Saul and Jonathan; only Saul and his son Jonathan had weapons.

units.leftText: The garrison of the Philistines went out to the pass of Michmash.
units.rightText: And a garrison of the Philistines had gone out to the pass at Michmash.

units.leftText: Now it happened on a day that Jonathan the son of Saul said to the young man who bore his armor, “Come! Let’s go over to the Philistines’ garrison that is on the other side.” But he didn’t tell his father.
units.rightText: One day Jonathan son of Saul said to the young man bearing his armor, “Come, let us cross over to the Philistine outpost on the other side.” But Jonathan did not tell his father.

units.leftText: Saul stayed in the uttermost part of Gibeah under the pomegranate tree which is in Migron; and the people who were with him were about six hundred men,
units.rightText: Meanwhile, Saul was staying under the pomegranate tree in Migron on the outskirts of Gibeah. And the troops who were with him numbered about six hundred men,
rightNotes: 14:2 Or around the rock of Rimmon or in the pomegranate cave; see Judges 20:45|JDG 20:45*, Judges 20:47, and Judges 21:13.

units.leftText: including Ahijah the son of Ahitub, Ichabod’s brother, the son of Phinehas, the son of Eli the priest of the LORD in Shiloh, wearing an ephod. The people didn’t know that Jonathan was gone.
units.rightText: including Ahijah, who was wearing an ephod. He was the son of Ichabod’s brother Ahitub son of Phinehas, the son of Eli the priest of the LORD in Shiloh. But the troops did not know that Jonathan had left.

units.leftText: Between the passes, by which Jonathan sought to go over to the Philistines’ garrison, there was a rocky crag on the one side and a rocky crag on the other side; and the name of the one was Bozez, and the name of the other Seneh.
units.rightText: Now there were cliffs on both sides of the pass that Jonathan intended to cross to reach the Philistine outpost. One was named Bozez and the other Seneh.

units.leftText: The one crag rose up on the north in front of Michmash, and the other on the south in front of Geba.
units.rightText: One cliff stood to the north toward Michmash, and the other to the south toward Geba.

units.leftText: Jonathan said to the young man who bore his armor, “Come! Let’s go over to the garrison of these uncircumcised. It may be that the LORD will work for us, for there is no restraint on the LORD to save by many or by few.”
units.rightText: Jonathan said to the young man bearing his armor, “Come, let us cross over to the outpost of these uncircumcised men. Perhaps the LORD will work on our behalf. Nothing can hinder the LORD from saving, whether by many or by few.”

units.leftText: His armor bearer said to him, “Do all that is in your heart. Go, and behold, I am with you according to your heart.”
units.rightText: His armor-bearer replied, “Do all that is in your heart. Go ahead; I am with you heart and soul.”

units.leftText: Then Jonathan said, “Behold, we will pass over to the men, and we will reveal ourselves to them.
units.rightText: “Very well,” said Jonathan, “we will cross over toward these men and show ourselves to them.

units.leftText: If they say this to us, ‘Wait until we come to you!’ then we will stand still in our place and will not go up to them.
units.rightText: If they say, ‘Wait until we come to you,’ then we will stay where we are and will not go up to them.

units.leftText: But if they say this, ‘Come up to us!’ then we will go up, for the LORD has delivered them into our hand. This shall be the sign to us.”
units.rightText: But if they say, ‘Come on up,’ then we will go up, because this will be our sign that the LORD has delivered them into our hands.”

units.leftText: Both of them revealed themselves to the garrison of the Philistines; and the Philistines said, “Behold, the Hebrews are coming out of the holes where they had hidden themselves!”
units.rightText: So the two of them showed themselves to the outpost of the Philistines, who exclaimed, “Look, the Hebrews are coming out of the holes in which they were hiding!”

units.leftText: The men of the garrison answered Jonathan and his armor bearer, and said, “Come up to us, and we will show you something!”
units.rightText: So the men of the outpost called out to Jonathan and his armor-bearer, “Come on up, and we will teach you a lesson!”

units.leftText: Jonathan climbed up on his hands and on his feet, and his armor bearer after him, and they fell before Jonathan; and his armor bearer killed them after him.
units.rightText: So Jonathan climbed up on his hands and feet, with his armor-bearer behind him. And the Philistines fell before Jonathan, and his armor-bearer followed and finished them off.

units.leftText: That first slaughter, which Jonathan and his armor bearer made, was about twenty men, within as it were half a furrow’s length in an acre of land.
units.rightText: In that first assault, Jonathan and his armor-bearer struck down about twenty men in about half an acre of land.
rightNotes: 14:14 Hebrew half a yoke. A yoke was the amount of land plowed by a pair of yoked oxen in one day.

units.leftText: There was a trembling in the camp, in the field, and among all the people; the garrison and the raiders also trembled; and the earth quaked, so there was an exceedingly great trembling.
units.rightText: Then panic struck the Philistines in the camp, in the field, and among all the people. Even those in the outposts and raiding parties trembled. Indeed, the earth quaked, and panic spread from God.
rightNotes: 14:15 Or and a terrible panic spread

units.leftText: The watchmen of Saul in Gibeah of Benjamin looked; and behold, the multitude melted away and scattered.
units.rightText: Now when Saul’s watchmen at Gibeah in Benjamin looked and saw the troops melting away and scattering in every direction,
rightNotes: 14:16 Or melting away and going here and there

units.leftText: Then Saul said to the people who were with him, “Count now, and see who is missing from us.” When they had counted, behold, Jonathan and his armor bearer were not there.
units.rightText: Saul said to the troops who were with him, “Call the roll and see who has left us.”

units.leftText: Saul said to Ahijah, “Bring God’s ark here.” For God’s ark was with the children of Israel at that time.
units.rightText: Then Saul said to Ahijah, “Bring the ark of God.” (For at that time it was with the Israelites.)
rightNotes: 14:18 Hebrew; LXX “Bring the ephod.” For at that time he wore the ephod before the Israelites.

units.leftText: While Saul talked to the priest, the tumult that was in the camp of the Philistines went on and increased; and Saul said to the priest, “Withdraw your hand!”
units.rightText: While Saul was talking to the priest, the commotion in the Philistine camp continued to increase. So Saul said to the priest, “Withdraw your hand.”

units.leftText: Saul and all the people who were with him were gathered together, and came to the battle; and behold, they were all striking each other with their swords in very great confusion.
units.rightText: Then Saul and all his troops assembled and marched to the battle, and they found the Philistines in total confusion, with each man wielding the sword against his neighbor.

units.leftText: Now the Hebrews who were with the Philistines before and who went up with them into the camp from all around, even they also turned to be with the Israelites who were with Saul and Jonathan.
units.rightText: And the Hebrews who had previously gone up into the surrounding camps to join the Philistines now went over to the Israelites who were with Saul and Jonathan.

units.leftText: Likewise all the men of Israel who had hidden themselves in the hill country of Ephraim, when they heard that the Philistines fled, even they also followed hard after them in the battle.
units.rightText: When all the Israelites who had been hiding in the hill country of Ephraim heard that the Philistines were fleeing, they also joined the battle in close pursuit.

units.leftText: So the LORD saved Israel that day; and the battle passed over by Beth Aven.
units.rightText: So the LORD saved Israel that day, and the battle moved on beyond Beth-aven.

units.leftText: The men of Israel were distressed that day; for Saul had adjured the people, saying, “Cursed is the man who eats any food until it is evening, and I am avenged of my enemies.” So none of the people tasted food.
units.rightText: Now the men of Israel were in distress that day, for Saul had placed the troops under an oath, saying, “Cursed is the man who eats any food before evening, before I have taken vengeance on my enemies.” So none of the troops tasted any food.

units.leftText: All the people came into the forest; and there was honey on the ground.
units.rightText: Then all the troops entered the forest, and there was honey on the ground.

units.leftText: When the people had come to the forest, behold, honey was dripping, but no one put his hand to his mouth, for the people feared the oath.
units.rightText: And when they entered the forest and saw the flowing honey, not one of them put his hand to his mouth, because they feared the oath.

units.leftText: But Jonathan didn’t hear when his father commanded the people with the oath. Therefore he put out the end of the rod that was in his hand and dipped it in the honeycomb, and put his hand to his mouth; and his eyes brightened.
units.rightText: Jonathan, however, had not heard that his father had bound the people with the oath. So he reached out the end of the staff in his hand, dipped it into the honeycomb, and put his hand to his mouth, and his eyes brightened.
rightNotes: 14:27 Or his strength was renewed; similarly in verse 29

units.leftText: Then one of the people answered, and said, “Your father directly commanded the people with an oath, saying, ‘Cursed is the man who eats food today.’” So the people were faint.
units.rightText: Then one of the soldiers told him, “Your father bound the troops with a solemn oath, saying, ‘Cursed is the man who eats food today.’ That is why the people are faint.”

units.leftText: Then Jonathan said, “My father has troubled the land. Please look how my eyes have brightened because I tasted a little of this honey.
units.rightText: “My father has brought trouble to the land,” Jonathan replied. “Just look at how my eyes have brightened because I tasted a little of this honey.

units.leftText: How much more, if perhaps the people had eaten freely today of the plunder of their enemies which they found? For now there has been no great slaughter among the Philistines.”
units.rightText: How much better it would have been if the troops had eaten freely today from the plunder they took from their enemies! Would not the slaughter of the Philistines have been much greater?”

units.leftText: They struck the Philistines that day from Michmash to Aijalon. The people were very faint;
units.rightText: That day, after the Israelites had struck down the Philistines from Michmash to Aijalon, the people were very faint.

units.leftText: and the people pounced on the plunder, and took sheep, cattle, and calves, and killed them on the ground; and the people ate them with the blood.
units.rightText: So they rushed greedily to the plunder, taking sheep, cattle, and calves. They slaughtered them on the ground and ate meat with the blood still in it.

units.leftText: Then they told Saul, saying, “Behold, the people are sinning against the LORD, in that they eat meat with the blood.”
units.rightText: Then someone reported to Saul: “Look, the troops are sinning against the LORD by eating meat with the blood still in it.”

units.leftText: Saul said, “Disperse yourselves among the people, and tell them, ‘Every man bring me here his ox, and every man his sheep, and kill them here, and eat; and don’t sin against the LORD in eating meat with the blood.’” All the people brought every man his ox with him that night, and killed them there.
units.rightText: Then he said, “Go among the troops and tell them, ‘Each man must bring me his ox or his sheep, slaughter them in this place, and then eat. Do not sin against the LORD by eating meat with the blood still in it.’”

units.leftText: Saul built an altar to the LORD. This was the first altar that he built to the LORD.
units.rightText: Then Saul built an altar to the LORD; it was the first time he had built an altar to the LORD.

units.leftText: Saul said, “Let’s go down after the Philistines by night, and take plunder among them until the morning light. Let’s not leave a man of them.”
units.rightText: And Saul said, “Let us go down after the Philistines by night and plunder them until dawn, leaving no man alive!”

units.leftText: Saul asked counsel of God: “Shall I go down after the Philistines? Will you deliver them into the hand of Israel?” But he didn’t answer him that day.
units.rightText: So Saul inquired of God, “Shall I go down after the Philistines? Will You give them into the hand of Israel?”

units.leftText: Saul said, “Draw near here, all you chiefs of the people, and know and see in whom this sin has been today.
units.rightText: Therefore Saul said, “Come here, all you leaders of the troops, and let us investigate how this sin has occurred today.

units.leftText: For as the LORD lives, who saves Israel, though it is in Jonathan my son, he shall surely die.” But there was not a man among all the people who answered him.
units.rightText: As surely as the LORD who saves Israel lives, even if it is my son Jonathan, he must die!”

units.leftText: Then he said to all Israel, “You be on one side, and I and Jonathan my son will be on the other side.”
units.rightText: Then Saul said to all Israel, “You stand on one side, and I and my son Jonathan will stand on the other side.”

units.leftText: Therefore Saul said to the LORD, the God of Israel, “Show the right.”
units.rightText: So Saul said to the LORD, the God of Israel, “Why have You not answered Your servant this day? If the fault is with me or my son Jonathan, respond with Urim, but if the fault is with the men of Israel, respond with Thummim.” And Jonathan and Saul were selected, but the people were cleared of the charge.
rightNotes: 14:41 LXX and Vulgate; MT contains only the short quotation, “Give a perfect (lot).”

units.leftText: Saul said, “Cast lots between me and Jonathan my son.”
units.rightText: Then Saul said, “Cast the lot between me and my son Jonathan.” And Jonathan was selected.

units.leftText: Then Saul said to Jonathan, “Tell me what you have done!”
units.rightText: “Tell me what you have done,” Saul commanded him.

units.leftText: Saul said, “God do so and more also; for you shall surely die, Jonathan.”
units.rightText: And Saul declared, “May God punish me, and ever so severely, if you, Jonathan, do not surely die!”

units.leftText: The people said to Saul, “Shall Jonathan die, who has worked this great salvation in Israel? Far from it! As the LORD lives, there shall not one hair of his head fall to the ground, for he has worked with God today!” So the people rescued Jonathan, so he didn’t die.
units.rightText: But the people said to Saul, “Must Jonathan die — he who accomplished such a great deliverance for Israel? Never! As surely as the LORD lives, not a hair of his head will fall to the ground, for with God’s help he has accomplished this today.”

units.leftText: Then Saul went up from following the Philistines; and the Philistines went to their own place.
units.rightText: Then Saul gave up his pursuit of the Philistines, and the Philistines returned to their own land.

units.leftText: Now when Saul had taken the kingdom over Israel, he fought against all his enemies on every side: against Moab, and against the children of Ammon, and against Edom, and against the kings of Zobah, and against the Philistines. Wherever he turned himself, he defeated them.
units.rightText: After Saul had assumed the kingship over Israel, he fought against all his enemies on every side — the Moabites, the Ammonites, the Edomites, the kings of Zobah, and the Philistines. Wherever he turned, he routed them.
rightNotes: 14:47 MT; DSS and LXX king
14:47 Or he inflicted punishment on them from Hebrew; LXX he was victorious

units.leftText: He did valiantly and struck the Amalekites, and delivered Israel out of the hands of those who plundered them.
units.rightText: He fought valiantly and defeated the Amalekites, delivering Israel from the hands of its plunderers.

units.leftText: Now the sons of Saul were Jonathan, Ishvi, and Malchishua; and the names of his two daughters were these: the name of the firstborn Merab, and the name of the younger Michal.
units.rightText: Now the sons of Saul were Jonathan, Ishvi, and Malchishua. His two daughters were named Merab (his firstborn) and Michal (his younger daughter).

units.leftText: The name of Saul’s wife was Ahinoam the daughter of Ahimaaz. The name of the captain of his army was Abner the son of Ner, Saul’s uncle.
units.rightText: His wife’s name was Ahinoam daughter of Ahimaaz. The name of the commander of his army was Abner, the son of Saul’s uncle Ner.

units.leftText: Kish was the father of Saul, and Ner the father of Abner was the son of Abiel.
units.rightText: Saul’s father Kish and Abner’s father Ner were sons of Abiel.

units.leftText: There was severe war against the Philistines all the days of Saul; and when Saul saw any mighty man or any valiant man, he took him into his service.
units.rightText: And the war with the Philistines was fierce for all the days of Saul. So whenever he noticed any strong or brave man, Saul would enlist him.

units.leftText: Samuel said to Saul, “The LORD sent me to anoint you to be king over his people, over Israel. Now therefore listen to the voice of the LORD’s words.
units.rightText: Then Samuel said to Saul, “The LORD sent me to anoint you king over His people Israel. Now therefore, listen to the words of the LORD.

units.leftText: The LORD of Armies says, ‘I remember what Amalek did to Israel, how he set himself against him on the way when he came up out of Egypt.
units.rightText: This is what the LORD of Hosts says: ‘I witnessed what the Amalekites did to the Israelites when they opposed them on their way up from Egypt.

units.leftText: Now go and strike Amalek, and utterly destroy all that they have, and don’t spare them; but kill both man and woman, infant and nursing baby, ox and sheep, camel and donkey.’”
units.rightText: Now go and attack the Amalekites and devote to destruction all that belongs to them. Do not spare them, but put to death men and women, children and infants, oxen and sheep, camels and donkeys.’”
rightNotes: 15:3 Forms of the Hebrew cherem refer to the giving over of things or persons to the LORD, either by destroying them or by giving them as an offering; also in verses 8, 9, 15, 18, 20, and 21.

units.leftText: Saul summoned the people, and counted them in Telaim, two hundred thousand footmen and ten thousand men of Judah.
units.rightText: So Saul summoned the troops and numbered them at Telaim — 200,000 foot soldiers and 10,000 men of Judah.

units.leftText: Saul came to the city of Amalek, and set an ambush in the valley.
units.rightText: Saul came to the city of Amalek and lay in wait in the valley.

units.leftText: Saul said to the Kenites, “Go, depart, go down from among the Amalekites, lest I destroy you with them; for you showed kindness to all the children of Israel when they came up out of Egypt.” So the Kenites departed from among the Amalekites.
units.rightText: And he warned the Kenites, “Since you showed kindness to all the Israelites when they came up out of Egypt, go on and get away from the Amalekites. Otherwise I will sweep you away with them.”

units.leftText: Saul struck the Amalekites, from Havilah as you go to Shur, which is before Egypt.
units.rightText: Then Saul struck down the Amalekites all the way from Havilah to Shur, which is east of Egypt.

units.leftText: He took Agag the king of the Amalekites alive, and utterly destroyed all the people with the edge of the sword.
units.rightText: He captured Agag king of Amalek alive, but devoted all the others to destruction with the sword.

units.leftText: But Saul and the people spared Agag and the best of the sheep, of the cattle, of the fat calves, of the lambs, and all that was good, and were not willing to utterly destroy them; but everything that was vile and refuse, that they destroyed utterly.
units.rightText: Saul and his troops spared Agag, along with the best of the sheep and cattle, the fat calves and lambs, and the best of everything else. They were unwilling to devote them to destruction, but they devoted to destruction all that was despised and worthless.
rightNotes: 15:9 Or the grown bulls

units.leftText: Then the LORD’s word came to Samuel, saying,
units.rightText: Then the word of the LORD came to Samuel, saying,

units.leftText: “It grieves me that I have set up Saul to be king, for he has turned back from following me, and has not performed my commandments.” Samuel was angry; and he cried to the LORD all night.
units.rightText: “I regret that I have made Saul king, for he has turned away from following Me and has not carried out My instructions.”

units.leftText: Samuel rose early to meet Saul in the morning; and Samuel was told, saying, “Saul came to Carmel, and behold, he set up a monument for himself, turned, passed on, and went down to Gilgal.”
units.rightText: Early in the morning Samuel got up to confront Saul, but he was told, “Saul has gone to Carmel, and behold, he has set up a monument for himself and has turned and gone down to Gilgal.”

units.leftText: Samuel came to Saul; and Saul said to him, “You are blessed by the LORD! I have performed the commandment of the LORD.”
units.rightText: When Samuel reached him, Saul said to him, “May the LORD bless you. I have carried out the LORD’s instructions.”

units.leftText: Samuel said, “Then what does this bleating of the sheep in my ears and the lowing of the cattle which I hear mean?”
units.rightText: But Samuel replied, “Then what is this bleating of sheep and lowing of cattle that I hear?”

units.leftText: Saul said, “They have brought them from the Amalekites; for the people spared the best of the sheep and of the cattle, to sacrifice to the LORD your God. We have utterly destroyed the rest.”
units.rightText: Saul answered, “The troops brought them from the Amalekites; they spared the best sheep and cattle to sacrifice to the LORD your God, but the rest we devoted to destruction.”

units.leftText: Then Samuel said to Saul, “Stay, and I will tell you what the LORD said to me last night.”
units.rightText: “Stop!” exclaimed Samuel. “Let me tell you what the LORD said to me last night.”

units.leftText: Samuel said, “Though you were little in your own sight, weren’t you made the head of the tribes of Israel? The LORD anointed you king over Israel;
units.rightText: And Samuel said, “Although you were once small in your own eyes, have you not become the head of the tribes of Israel? The LORD anointed you king over Israel

units.leftText: and the LORD sent you on a journey, and said, ‘Go, and utterly destroy the sinners the Amalekites, and fight against them until they are consumed.’
units.rightText: and sent you on a mission, saying, ‘Go and devote to destruction the sinful Amalekites. Fight against them until you have wiped them out.’

units.leftText: Why then didn’t you obey the LORD’s voice, but took the plunder, and did that which was evil in the LORD’s sight?”
units.rightText: So why did you not obey the LORD? Why did you rush upon the plunder and do evil in the sight of the LORD?”

units.leftText: Saul said to Samuel, “But I have obeyed the LORD’s voice, and have gone the way which the LORD sent me, and have brought Agag the king of Amalek, and have utterly destroyed the Amalekites.
units.rightText: “But I did obey the LORD,” Saul replied. “I went on the mission that the LORD gave me. I brought back Agag king of Amalek and devoted the Amalekites to destruction.

units.leftText: But the people took of the plunder, sheep and cattle, the best of the devoted things, to sacrifice to the LORD your God in Gilgal.”
units.rightText: The troops took sheep and cattle from the plunder, the best of the things devoted to destruction, in order to sacrifice them to the LORD your God at Gilgal.”

units.leftText: Samuel said, “Has the LORD as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the LORD’s voice? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to listen than the fat of rams.
units.rightText: But Samuel declared:

units.leftText: For rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft, and stubbornness is as idolatry and teraphim. Because you have rejected the LORD’s word, he has also rejected you from being king.”
units.rightText: For rebellion is like the sin of divination,
leftNotes: 15:23 teraphim were household idols that may have been associated with inheritance rights to the household property.

units.leftText: Saul said to Samuel, “I have sinned; for I have transgressed the commandment of the LORD and your words, because I feared the people and obeyed their voice.
units.rightText: Then Saul said to Samuel, “I have sinned; I have transgressed the LORD’s commandment and your instructions, because I feared the people and obeyed their voice.

units.leftText: Now therefore, please pardon my sin, and turn again with me, that I may worship the LORD.”
units.rightText: Now therefore, please forgive my sin and return with me so I can worship the LORD.”

units.leftText: Samuel said to Saul, “I will not return with you; for you have rejected the LORD’s word, and the LORD has rejected you from being king over Israel.”
units.rightText: “I will not return with you,” Samuel replied. “For you have rejected the word of the LORD, and He has rejected you as king over Israel.”

units.leftText: As Samuel turned around to go away, Saul grabbed the skirt of his robe, and it tore.
units.rightText: As Samuel turned to go, Saul grabbed the hem of his robe, and it tore.

units.leftText: Samuel said to him, “The LORD has torn the kingdom of Israel from you today, and has given it to a neighbor of yours who is better than you.
units.rightText: So Samuel said to him, “The LORD has torn the kingdom of Israel from you today and has given it to your neighbor who is better than you.

units.leftText: Also the Strength of Israel will not lie nor repent; for he is not a man, that he should repent.”
units.rightText: Moreover, the Glory of Israel does not lie or change His mind, for He is not a man, that He should change His mind.”

units.leftText: Then he said, “I have sinned; yet please honor me now before the elders of my people and before Israel, and come back with me, that I may worship the LORD your God.”
units.rightText: “I have sinned,” Saul replied. “Please honor me now before the elders of my people and before Israel. Come back with me, so that I may worship the LORD your God.”

units.leftText: So Samuel went back with Saul; and Saul worshiped the LORD.
units.rightText: So Samuel went back with Saul, and Saul worshiped the LORD.

units.leftText: Then Samuel said, “Bring Agag the king of the Amalekites here to me!”
units.rightText: Then Samuel said, “Bring me Agag king of the Amalekites.”

units.leftText: Samuel said, “As your sword has made women childless, so your mother will be childless among women!” Then Samuel cut Agag in pieces before the LORD in Gilgal.
units.rightText: But Samuel declared:

units.leftText: Then Samuel went to Ramah; and Saul went up to his house to Gibeah of Saul.
units.rightText: Then Samuel went to Ramah, but Saul went up to his home in Gibeah of Saul.

units.leftText: Samuel came no more to see Saul until the day of his death, but Samuel mourned for Saul. The LORD grieved that he had made Saul king over Israel.
units.rightText: And to the day of his death, Samuel never again visited Saul. Samuel mourned for Saul, and the LORD regretted that He had made Saul king over Israel.

units.leftText: The LORD said to Samuel, “How long will you mourn for Saul, since I have rejected him from being king over Israel? Fill your horn with oil, and go. I will send you to Jesse the Bethlehemite, for I have provided a king for myself among his sons.”
units.rightText: Now the LORD said to Samuel, “How long are you going to mourn for Saul, since I have rejected him as king over Israel? Fill your horn with oil and go. I am sending you to Jesse of Bethlehem, for I have selected from his sons a king for Myself.”

units.leftText: Samuel said, “How can I go? If Saul hears it, he will kill me.”
units.rightText: “How can I go?” Samuel asked. “Saul will hear of it and kill me!”

units.leftText: Call Jesse to the sacrifice, and I will show you what you shall do. You shall anoint to me him whom I name to you.”
units.rightText: Then invite Jesse to the sacrifice, and I will show you what you are to do. You are to anoint for Me the one I indicate.”

units.leftText: Samuel did that which the LORD spoke, and came to Bethlehem. The elders of the city came to meet him trembling, and said, “Do you come peaceably?”
units.rightText: So Samuel did what the LORD had said and went to Bethlehem. When the elders of the town met him, they trembled and asked, “Do you come in peace?”

units.leftText: He said, “Peaceably; I have come to sacrifice to the LORD. Sanctify yourselves, and come with me to the sacrifice.” He sanctified Jesse and his sons, and called them to the sacrifice.
units.rightText: “In peace,” he replied. “I have come to sacrifice to the LORD. Consecrate yourselves and come with me to the sacrifice.”

units.leftText: When they had come, he looked at Eliab, and said, “Surely the LORD’s anointed is before him.”
units.rightText: When they arrived, Samuel saw Eliab and said, “Surely here before the LORD is His anointed.”

units.leftText: But the LORD said to Samuel, “Don’t look on his face, or on the height of his stature, because I have rejected him; for I don’t see as man sees. For man looks at the outward appearance, but the LORD looks at the heart.”
units.rightText: But the LORD said to Samuel, “Do not consider his appearance or height, for I have rejected him; the LORD does not see as man does. For man sees the outward appearance, but the LORD sees the heart.”

units.leftText: Then Jesse called Abinadab, and made him pass before Samuel. He said, “The LORD has not chosen this one, either.”
units.rightText: Then Jesse called Abinadab and presented him to Samuel, who said, “The LORD has not chosen this one either.”

units.leftText: Then Jesse made Shammah to pass by. He said, “The LORD has not chosen this one, either.”
units.rightText: Next Jesse presented Shammah, but Samuel said, “The LORD has not chosen this one either.”
rightNotes: 16:9 Shammah is a variant of Shimeah, Shimea, and Shimei; see 2 Samuel 13:3|2SA 13:3*, 2 Samuel 21:21, and 1 Chronicles 2:13.

units.leftText: Jesse made seven of his sons to pass before Samuel. Samuel said to Jesse, “The LORD has not chosen these.”
units.rightText: Thus Jesse made seven of his sons pass before Samuel, but Samuel told him, “The LORD has not chosen any of these.”

units.leftText: Samuel said to Jesse, “Are all your children here?”
units.rightText: And Samuel asked him, “Are these all the sons you have?”

units.leftText: He sent, and brought him in. Now he was ruddy, with a handsome face and good appearance. The LORD said, “Arise! Anoint him, for this is he.”
units.rightText: So Jesse sent for his youngest son and brought him in. He was ruddy, with beautiful eyes and a handsome appearance. And the LORD said, “Rise and anoint him, for he is the one.”

units.leftText: Then Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him in the middle of his brothers. Then the LORD’s Spirit came mightily on David from that day forward. So Samuel rose up and went to Ramah.
units.rightText: So Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him in the presence of his brothers, and the Spirit of the LORD rushed upon David from that day forward. Then Samuel set out and went to Ramah.

units.leftText: Now the LORD’s Spirit departed from Saul, and an evil spirit from the LORD troubled him.
units.rightText: Now the Spirit of the LORD departed from Saul, and a spirit of distress from the LORD began to torment him.
rightNotes: 16:14 Or a harmful spirit; similarly in verses 15, 16, and 23

units.leftText: Saul’s servants said to him, “See now, an evil spirit from God troubles you.
units.rightText: Saul’s servants said to him, “Surely a spirit of distress from God is tormenting you.

units.leftText: Let our lord now command your servants who are in front of you to seek out a man who is a skillful player on the harp. Then when the evil spirit from God is on you, he will play with his hand, and you will be well.”
units.rightText: Let our lord command your servants here to seek out someone who can skillfully play the harp. Whenever the spirit of distress from God is upon you, he is to play it, and you will be well.”

units.leftText: Saul said to his servants, “Provide me now a man who can play well, and bring him to me.”
units.rightText: And Saul commanded his servants, “Find me someone who plays well, and bring him to me.”

units.leftText: Then one of the young men answered and said, “Behold, I have seen a son of Jesse the Bethlehemite who is skillful in playing, a mighty man of valor, a man of war, prudent in speech, and a handsome person; and the LORD is with him.”
units.rightText: One of the servants answered, “I have seen a son of Jesse of Bethlehem who knows how to play the harp. He is a mighty man of valor, a warrior, eloquent and handsome, and the LORD is with him.”

units.leftText: Therefore Saul sent messengers to Jesse, and said, “Send me David your son, who is with the sheep.”
units.rightText: So Saul sent messengers to Jesse and said, “Send me your son David, who is with the sheep.”

units.leftText: Jesse took a donkey loaded with bread, a container of wine, and a young goat, and sent them by David his son to Saul.
units.rightText: And Jesse took a donkey loaded with bread, a skin of wine, and one young goat and sent them to Saul with his son David.

units.leftText: David came to Saul and stood before him. He loved him greatly; and he became his armor bearer.
units.rightText: When David came to Saul and entered his service, Saul loved him very much, and David became his armor-bearer.

units.leftText: Saul sent to Jesse, saying, “Please let David stand before me, for he has found favor in my sight.”
units.rightText: Then Saul sent word to Jesse, saying, “Let David remain in my service, for I am pleased with him.”

units.leftText: When the spirit from God was on Saul, David took the harp and played with his hand; so Saul was refreshed and was well, and the evil spirit departed from him.
units.rightText: And whenever the spirit from God came upon Saul, David would pick up his harp and play. Then Saul would find relief and feel better, and the spirit of distress would depart from him.

units.leftText: Now the Philistines gathered together their armies to battle; and they were gathered together at Socoh, which belongs to Judah, and encamped between Socoh and Azekah in Ephesdammim.
units.rightText: Now the Philistines gathered their forces for war at Socoh in Judah, and they camped between Socoh and Azekah in Ephes-dammim.

units.leftText: Saul and the men of Israel were gathered together, and encamped in the valley of Elah, and set the battle in array against the Philistines.
units.rightText: Saul and the men of Israel assembled and camped in the Valley of Elah, arraying themselves for battle against the Philistines.

units.leftText: The Philistines stood on the mountain on the one side, and Israel stood on the mountain on the other side: and there was a valley between them.
units.rightText: The Philistines stood on one hill and the Israelites stood on another, with the valley between them.

units.leftText: A champion out of the camp of the Philistines named Goliath of Gath, whose height was six cubits and a span went out.
units.rightText: Then a champion named Goliath, who was from Gath, came out from the Philistine camp. He was six cubits and a span in height,
leftNotes: 17:4 A cubit is the length from the tip of the middle finger to the elbow on a man’s arm, or about 18 inches or 46 centimeters. A span is the length from the tip of a man’s thumb to the tip of his little finger when his hand is stretched out (about half a cubit, or 9 inches, or 22.8 cm.) Therefore, Goliath was about 9 feet and 9 inches or 2.97 meters tall.
rightNotes: 17:4 Goliath was approximately 9 feet 9 inches or 297 centimeters tall; LXX, DSS, and Josephus four cubits and a span in height (approximately 6 feet 9 inches or 206 centimeters tall).

units.leftText: He had a helmet of bronze on his head, and he wore a coat of mail; and the weight of the coat was five thousand shekels of bronze.
units.rightText: and he had a bronze helmet on his head. He wore a bronze coat of mail weighing five thousand shekels,
leftNotes: 17:5 A shekel is about 10 grams or about 0.35 ounces, so 5000 shekels is about 50 kilograms or 110 pounds.
rightNotes: 17:5 5,000 shekels is approximately 125.6 pounds or 57 kilograms.

units.leftText: He had bronze shin armor on his legs and a bronze javelin between his shoulders.
units.rightText: and he had armor of bronze on his legs and a javelin of bronze slung between his shoulders.

units.leftText: The staff of his spear was like a weaver’s beam; and his spear’s head weighed six hundred shekels of iron. His shield bearer went before him.
units.rightText: The shaft of his spear was like a weaver’s beam, and its iron point weighed six hundred shekels. In addition, his shield bearer went before him.
leftNotes: 17:7 A shekel is about 10 grams or about 0.35 ounces, so 600 shekels is about 6 kilograms or about 13 pounds.
rightNotes: 17:7 600 shekels is approximately 15.1 pounds or 6.8 kilograms.

units.leftText: He stood and cried to the armies of Israel, and said to them, “Why have you come out to set your battle in array? Am I not a Philistine, and you servants to Saul? Choose a man for yourselves, and let him come down to me.
units.rightText: And Goliath stood and shouted to the ranks of Israel, “Why do you come out and array yourselves for battle? Am I not a Philistine, and are you not servants of Saul? Choose one of your men and have him come down against me.

units.leftText: If he is able to fight with me and kill me, then will we be your servants; but if I prevail against him and kill him, then you will be our servants and serve us.”
units.rightText: If he is able to fight me and kill me, then we will be your servants. But if I prevail against him and kill him, then you shall be our servants and work for us.”

units.leftText: The Philistine said, “I defy the armies of Israel today! Give me a man, that we may fight together!”
units.rightText: Then the Philistine said, “I defy the ranks of Israel this day! Give me a man to fight!”

units.leftText: When Saul and all Israel heard those words of the Philistine, they were dismayed and greatly afraid.
units.rightText: On hearing the words of the Philistine, Saul and all the Israelites were dismayed and greatly afraid.

units.leftText: Now David was the son of that Ephrathite of Bethlehem Judah, whose name was Jesse; and he had eight sons. The man was an elderly old man in the days of Saul.
units.rightText: Now David was the son of a man named Jesse, an Ephrathite from Bethlehem of Judah who had eight sons. And in the days of Saul, Jesse was old and well along in years.
rightNotes: 17:12 LXX and Syriac; Hebrew he had become advanced among men

units.leftText: The three oldest sons of Jesse had gone after Saul to the battle; and the names of his three sons who went to the battle were Eliab the firstborn, and next to him Abinadab, and the third Shammah.
units.rightText: The three older sons of Jesse had followed Saul into battle: The firstborn was Eliab, the second was Abinadab, and the third was Shammah.

units.leftText: David was the youngest; and the three oldest followed Saul.
units.rightText: And David was the youngest.

units.leftText: Now David went back and forth from Saul to feed his father’s sheep at Bethlehem.
units.rightText: but David went back and forth from Saul to tend his father’s sheep in Bethlehem.

units.leftText: The Philistine came near morning and evening, and presented himself forty days.
units.rightText: For forty days the Philistine came forward every morning and evening to take his stand.

units.leftText: Jesse said to David his son, “Now take for your brothers an ephah of this parched grain and these ten loaves, and carry them quickly to the camp to your brothers;
units.rightText: One day Jesse said to his son David, “Take this ephah of roasted grain and these ten loaves of bread for your brothers and hurry to their camp.
leftNotes: 17:17 1 ephah is about 22 liters or about 2/3 of a bushel
rightNotes: 17:17 An ephah is approximately 20 dry quarts or 22 liters of roasted grain.

units.leftText: and bring these ten cheeses to the captain of their thousand; and see how your brothers are doing, and bring back news.”
units.rightText: Take also these ten portions of cheese to the commander of their unit. Check on the welfare of your brothers and bring back an assurance from them.
rightNotes: 17:18 Or some token from them or some pledge from them

units.leftText: Now Saul, and they, and all the men of Israel were in the valley of Elah, fighting with the Philistines.
units.rightText: They are with Saul and all the men of Israel in the Valley of Elah, fighting against the Philistines.”

units.leftText: David rose up early in the morning and left the sheep with a keeper, and took the provisions and went, as Jesse had commanded him. He came to the place of the wagons as the army which was going out to the fight shouted for the battle.
units.rightText: So David got up early in the morning, left the flock with a keeper, loaded up, and set out as Jesse had instructed him. He reached the camp as the army was marching out to its position and shouting the battle cry.

units.leftText: Israel and the Philistines put the battle in array, army against army.
units.rightText: And Israel and the Philistines arrayed in formation against each other.

units.leftText: David left his baggage in the hand of the keeper of the baggage and ran to the army, and came and greeted his brothers.
units.rightText: Then David left his supplies in the care of the quartermaster and ran to the battle line. When he arrived, he asked his brothers how they were doing.

units.leftText: As he talked with them, behold, the champion, the Philistine of Gath, Goliath by name, came up out of the ranks of the Philistines, and said the same words; and David heard them.
units.rightText: And as he was speaking with them, suddenly the champion named Goliath, the Philistine from Gath, came forward from the ranks of the Philistines and shouted his usual words, which David also heard.

units.leftText: All the men of Israel, when they saw the man, fled from him and were terrified.
units.rightText: When all the men of Israel saw Goliath, they fled from him in great fear.

units.leftText: The men of Israel said, “Have you seen this man who has come up? He has surely come up to defy Israel. The king will give great riches to the man who kills him, and will give him his daughter, and will make his father’s house tax-free in Israel.”
units.rightText: Now the men of Israel had been saying, “Do you see how this man keeps coming out to defy Israel? To the man who kills him the king will give great riches. And he will give him his daughter in marriage and exempt his father’s house from taxation in Israel.”

units.leftText: David spoke to the men who stood by him, saying, “What shall be done to the man who kills this Philistine and takes away the reproach from Israel? For who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should defy the armies of the living God?”
units.rightText: David asked the men who were standing with him, “What will be done for the man who kills this Philistine and removes this disgrace from Israel? Just who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should defy the armies of the living God?”

units.leftText: The people answered him in this way, saying, “So shall it be done to the man who kills him.”
units.rightText: The people told him about the offer, saying, “That is what will be done for the man who kills him.”

units.leftText: Eliab his oldest brother heard when he spoke to the men; and Eliab’s anger burned against David, and he said, “Why have you come down? With whom have you left those few sheep in the wilderness? I know your pride and the evil of your heart; for you have come down that you might see the battle.”
units.rightText: Now when David’s oldest brother Eliab heard him speaking to the men, his anger burned against David. “Why have you come down here?” he asked. “And with whom did you leave those few sheep in the wilderness? I know your pride and wickedness of heart — you have come down to see the battle!”

units.leftText: David said, “What have I now done? Is there not a cause?”
units.rightText: “What have I done now?” said David. “Was it not just a question?”

units.leftText: He turned away from him toward another, and spoke like that again; and the people answered him again the same way.
units.rightText: Then he turned from him toward another and asked about the offer, and those people answered him just as the first ones had answered.

units.leftText: When the words were heard which David spoke, they rehearsed them before Saul; and he sent for him.
units.rightText: Now David’s words were overheard and reported to Saul, who sent for him.

units.leftText: David said to Saul, “Let no man’s heart fail because of him. Your servant will go and fight with this Philistine.”
units.rightText: And David said to Saul, “Let no man’s heart fail on account of this Philistine. Your servant will go and fight him!”

units.leftText: Saul said to David, “You are not able to go against this Philistine to fight with him; for you are but a youth, and he a man of war from his youth.”
units.rightText: But Saul replied, “You cannot go out against this Philistine to fight him. You are just a boy, and he has been a warrior from his youth.”

units.leftText: David said to Saul, “Your servant was keeping his father’s sheep; and when a lion or a bear came and took a lamb out of the flock,
units.rightText: David replied, “Your servant has been tending his father’s sheep, and whenever a lion or a bear came and carried off a lamb from the flock,

units.leftText: I went out after him, struck him, and rescued it out of his mouth. When he arose against me, I caught him by his beard, struck him, and killed him.
units.rightText: I went after it, struck it down, and delivered the lamb from its mouth. If it reared up against me, I would grab it by its fur, strike it down, and kill it.

units.leftText: Your servant struck both the lion and the bear. This uncircumcised Philistine shall be as one of them, since he has defied the armies of the living God.”
units.rightText: Your servant has killed lions and bears; this uncircumcised Philistine will be like one of them, for he has defied the armies of the living God.”

units.leftText: David said, “The LORD, who delivered me out of the paw of the lion and out of the paw of the bear, will deliver me out of the hand of this Philistine.”
units.rightText: David added, “The LORD, who delivered me from the claws of the lion and the bear, will deliver me from the hand of this Philistine.”

units.leftText: Saul dressed David with his clothing. He put a helmet of bronze on his head, and he clad him with a coat of mail.
units.rightText: Then Saul clothed David in his own tunic, put a bronze helmet on his head, and dressed him in armor.

units.leftText: David strapped his sword on his clothing and he tried to move, for he had not tested it. David said to Saul, “I can’t go with these, for I have not tested them.” Then David took them off.
units.rightText: David strapped his sword over the tunic and tried to walk, but he was not accustomed to them.

units.leftText: He took his staff in his hand, and chose for himself five smooth stones out of the brook, and put them in the pouch of his shepherd’s bag which he had. His sling was in his hand; and he came near to the Philistine.
units.rightText: And David took his staff in his hand, selected five smooth stones from the brook, and put them in the pouch of his shepherd’s bag. And with his sling in hand, he approached the Philistine.

units.leftText: The Philistine walked and came near to David; and the man who bore the shield went before him.
units.rightText: Now the Philistine came closer and closer to David, with his shield-bearer before him.

units.leftText: When the Philistine looked around and saw David, he disdained him; for he was but a youth, and ruddy, and had a good looking face.
units.rightText: When the Philistine looked and saw David, he despised him because he was just a boy, ruddy and handsome.

units.leftText: The Philistine said to David, “Am I a dog, that you come to me with sticks?” The Philistine cursed David by his gods.
units.rightText: “Am I a dog,” he said to David, “that you come at me with sticks?” And the Philistine cursed David by his gods.

units.leftText: The Philistine said to David, “Come to me, and I will give your flesh to the birds of the sky and to the animals of the field.”
units.rightText: “Come here,” he called to David, “and I will give your flesh to the birds of the air and the beasts of the field!”

units.leftText: Then David said to the Philistine, “You come to me with a sword, with a spear, and with a javelin; but I come to you in the name of the LORD of Armies, the God of the armies of Israel, whom you have defied.
units.rightText: But David said to the Philistine, “You come against me with sword and spear and javelin, but I come against you in the name of the LORD of Hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom you have defied.

units.leftText: Today, the LORD will deliver you into my hand. I will strike you and take your head from off you. I will give the dead bodies of the army of the Philistines today to the birds of the sky and to the wild animals of the earth, that all the earth may know that there is a God in Israel,
units.rightText: This day the LORD will deliver you into my hand. This day I will strike you down, cut off your head, and give the carcasses of the Philistine army to the birds of the air and the creatures of the earth. Then the whole world will know that there is a God in Israel.

units.leftText: and that all this assembly may know that the LORD doesn’t save with sword and spear; for the battle is the LORD’s, and he will give you into our hand.”
units.rightText: And all those assembled here will know that it is not by sword or spear that the LORD saves; for the battle is the LORD’s, and He will give all of you into our hands.”

units.leftText: When the Philistine arose, and walked and came near to meet David, David hurried and ran toward the army to meet the Philistine.
units.rightText: As the Philistine started forward to attack him, David ran quickly toward the battle line to meet him.

units.leftText: David put his hand in his bag, took a stone and slung it, and struck the Philistine in his forehead. The stone sank into his forehead, and he fell on his face to the earth.
units.rightText: Then David reached into his bag, took out a stone, and slung it, striking the Philistine on the forehead. The stone sank into his forehead, and he fell facedown on the ground.

units.leftText: So David prevailed over the Philistine with a sling and with a stone, and struck the Philistine and killed him; but there was no sword in David’s hand.
units.rightText: Thus David prevailed over the Philistine with a sling and a stone; without a sword in his hand he struck down the Philistine and killed him.

units.leftText: Then David ran, stood over the Philistine, took his sword, drew it out of its sheath, killed him, and cut off his head with it.
units.rightText: David ran and stood over him. He grabbed the Philistine’s sword and pulled it from its sheath and killed him, and he cut off his head with the sword.

units.leftText: The men of Israel and of Judah arose and shouted, and pursued the Philistines as far as Gai and to the gates of Ekron. The wounded of the Philistines fell down by the way to Shaaraim, even to Gath and to Ekron.
units.rightText: Then the men of Israel and Judah charged forward with a shout and pursued the Philistines to the entrance of Gath and to the gates of Ekron. And the bodies of the Philistines were strewn along the Shaaraim road to Gath and Ekron.
rightNotes: 17:52 LXX; Hebrew of Gai; that is, of the valley

units.leftText: The children of Israel returned from chasing after the Philistines, and they plundered their camp.
units.rightText: When the Israelites returned from their pursuit of the Philistines, they plundered their camps.

units.leftText: David took the head of the Philistine and brought it to Jerusalem, but he put his armor in his tent.
units.rightText: David took the head of the Philistine and brought it to Jerusalem, and he put Goliath’s weapons in his own tent.

units.leftText: When Saul saw David go out against the Philistine, he said to Abner, the captain of the army, “Abner, whose son is this youth?”
units.rightText: As Saul had watched David going out to confront the Philistine, he said to Abner the commander of the army, “Abner, whose son is this young man?”

units.leftText: The king said, “Inquire whose son the young man is!”
units.rightText: “Find out whose son this young man is!” said the king.

units.leftText: As David returned from the slaughter of the Philistine, Abner took him and brought him before Saul with the head of the Philistine in his hand.
units.rightText: So when David returned from killing the Philistine, still holding his head in his hand, Abner took him and brought him before Saul.

units.leftText: Saul said to him, “Whose son are you, you young man?”
units.rightText: “Whose son are you, young man?” asked Saul.
