units.leftText: Now therefore what is under your hand? Please give me five loaves of bread in my hand, or whatever is available.”
units.rightText: Now then, what do you have on hand? Give me five loaves of bread, or whatever can be found.”

units.leftText: The priest answered David, and said, “I have no common bread, but there is holy bread; if only the young men have kept themselves from women.”
units.rightText: “There is no common bread on hand,” the priest replied, “but there is some consecrated bread — provided that the young men have kept themselves from women.”

units.leftText: David answered the priest, and said to him, “Truly, women have been kept from us as usual these three days. When I came out, the vessels of the young men were holy, though it was only a common journey. How much more then today shall their vessels be holy?”
units.rightText: David answered, “Women have indeed been kept from us, as is usual when I set out. And the bodies of the young men are holy even on common missions. How much more so today!”

units.leftText: So the priest gave him holy bread; for there was no bread there but the show bread that was taken from before the LORD, to be replaced with hot bread in the day when it was taken away.
units.rightText: So the priest gave him the consecrated bread, since there was no bread there but the Bread of the Presence, which had been removed from before the LORD and replaced with hot bread on the day it was taken away.

units.leftText: Now a certain man of the servants of Saul was there that day, detained before the LORD; and his name was Doeg the Edomite, the best of the herdsmen who belonged to Saul.
units.rightText: Now one of Saul’s servants was there that day, detained before the LORD. And his name was Doeg the Edomite, the chief shepherd for Saul.

units.leftText: David said to Ahimelech, “Isn’t there here under your hand spear or sword? For I haven’t brought my sword or my weapons with me, because the king’s business required haste.”
units.rightText: Then David asked Ahimelech, “Is there not a spear or sword on hand here? For I have brought neither my sword nor my weapons with me, because the king’s mission was urgent.”

units.leftText: The priest said, “Behold, the sword of Goliath the Philistine, whom you killed in the valley of Elah, is here wrapped in a cloth behind the ephod. If you would like to take that, take it, for there is no other except that here.”
units.rightText: The priest replied, “The sword of Goliath the Philistine, whom you killed in the Valley of Elah, is here; it is wrapped in a cloth behind the ephod. If you want, you may take it. For there is no other but this one here.”

units.leftText: David arose and fled that day for fear of Saul, and went to Achish the king of Gath.
units.rightText: That day David fled from Saul and went to Achish king of Gath.

units.leftText: The servants of Achish said to him, “Isn’t this David the king of the land? Didn’t they sing to one another about him in dances, saying,
units.rightText: But the servants of Achish said to him, “Is this not David, the king of the land? Did they not sing about him in their dances, saying:

units.leftText: David laid up these words in his heart, and was very afraid of Achish the king of Gath.
units.rightText: Now David took these words to heart and was very much afraid of Achish the king of Gath.

units.leftText: He changed his behavior before them and pretended to be insane in their hands, and scribbled on the doors of the gate, and let his spittle fall down on his beard.
units.rightText: So he changed his behavior before them and feigned madness in their hands; he scratched on the doors of the gate and let his saliva run down his beard.

units.leftText: Then Achish said to his servants, “Look, you see the man is insane. Why then have you brought him to me?
units.rightText: Then Achish said to his servants, “Look, you can see that the man is insane! Why have you brought him to me?

units.leftText: Do I lack madmen, that you have brought this fellow to play the madman in my presence? Should this fellow come into my house?”
units.rightText: Am I in need of madmen, that you have brought this man to rave in my presence? Must this man come into my house?”

units.leftText: David therefore departed from there and escaped to Adullam’s cave. When his brothers and all his father’s house heard it, they went down there to him.
units.rightText: So David left Gath and took refuge in the cave of Adullam. When his brothers and the rest of his father’s household heard about it, they went down to him there.

units.leftText: Everyone who was in distress, everyone who was in debt, and everyone who was discontented gathered themselves to him; and he became captain over them. There were with him about four hundred men.
units.rightText: And all who were distressed or indebted or discontented rallied around him, and he became their leader. About four hundred men were with him.

units.leftText: David went from there to Mizpeh of Moab; and he said to the king of Moab, “Please let my father and my mother come out to you, until I know what God will do for me.”
units.rightText: From there David went to Mizpeh of Moab, where he said to the king of Moab, “Please let my father and mother stay with you until I learn what God will do for me.”
rightNotes: 22:3 Syriac and Vulgate; Hebrew go forth

units.leftText: He brought them before the king of Moab; and they lived with him all the time that David was in the stronghold.
units.rightText: So he left them in the care of the king of Moab, and they stayed with him the whole time David was in the stronghold.

units.leftText: The prophet Gad said to David, “Don’t stay in the stronghold. Depart, and go into the land of Judah.”
units.rightText: Then the prophet Gad said to David, “Do not stay in the stronghold. Depart and go into the land of Judah.” So David left and went to the forest of Hereth.

units.leftText: Saul heard that David was discovered, with the men who were with him. Now Saul was sitting in Gibeah, under the tamarisk tree in Ramah, with his spear in his hand, and all his servants were standing around him.
units.rightText: Soon Saul learned that David and his men had been discovered. At that time Saul was sitting under the tamarisk tree on the hill at Gibeah, with his spear in hand and all his servants standing around him.

units.leftText: Saul said to his servants who stood around him, “Hear now, you Benjamites! Will the son of Jesse give everyone of you fields and vineyards? Will he make you all captains of thousands and captains of hundreds?
units.rightText: Then Saul said to his servants, “Listen, men of Benjamin! Is the son of Jesse giving all of you fields and vineyards and making you commanders of thousands or hundreds?

units.leftText: Is that why all of you have conspired against me, and there is no one who discloses to me when my son makes a treaty with the son of Jesse, and there is none of you who is sorry for me, or discloses to me that my son has stirred up my servant against me, to lie in wait, as it is today?”
units.rightText: Is that why all of you have conspired against me? Not one of you told me that my own son had made a covenant with the son of Jesse. Not one of you has shown concern for me or revealed to me that my son has stirred up my own servant to lie in wait against me, as is the case today.”

units.leftText: Then Doeg the Edomite, who stood by the servants of Saul, answered and said, “I saw the son of Jesse coming to Nob, to Ahimelech the son of Ahitub.
units.rightText: But Doeg the Edomite, who had stationed himself with Saul’s servants, answered: “I saw the son of Jesse come to Ahimelech son of Ahitub at Nob.

units.leftText: He inquired of the LORD for him, gave him food, and gave him the sword of Goliath the Philistine.”
units.rightText: Ahimelech inquired of the LORD for him and gave him provisions. He also gave him the sword of Goliath the Philistine.”

units.leftText: Then the king sent to call Ahimelech the priest, the son of Ahitub, and all his father’s house, the priests who were in Nob; and they all came to the king.
units.rightText: Then the king sent messengers to summon Ahimelech the priest, the son of Ahitub, and his father’s whole family, who were priests at Nob. And all of them came to the king.

units.leftText: Saul said, “Hear now, you son of Ahitub.”
units.rightText: “Listen now, son of Ahitub,” said Saul.

units.leftText: Saul said to him, “Why have you conspired against me, you and the son of Jesse, in that you have given him bread, and a sword, and have inquired of God for him, that he should rise against me, to lie in wait, as it is today?”
units.rightText: And Saul asked him, “Why have you and the son of Jesse conspired against me? You gave him bread and a sword and inquired of God for him so that he could rise up against me to lie in wait, as he is doing today.”

units.leftText: Then Ahimelech answered the king, and said, “Who among all your servants is so faithful as David, who is the king’s son-in-law, captain of your body guard, and honored in your house?
units.rightText: Ahimelech answered the king, “Who among all your servants is as faithful as David, the king’s son-in-law, the captain of your bodyguard and honored in your house?

units.leftText: Have I today begun to inquire of God for him? Be it far from me! Don’t let the king impute anything to his servant, nor to all the house of my father; for your servant knew nothing of all this, less or more.”
units.rightText: Was that day the first time I inquired of God for him? Far be it from me! Let not the king accuse your servant or any of my father’s household, for your servant knew nothing of this whole affair — not in part or in whole.”

units.leftText: The king said, “You shall surely die, Ahimelech, you and all your father’s house.”
units.rightText: But the king replied, “You will surely die, Ahimelech, you and all your father’s house!”

units.leftText: The king said to the guard who stood about him, “Turn and kill the priests of the LORD, because their hand also is with David, and because they knew that he fled and didn’t disclose it to me.” But the servants of the king wouldn’t put out their hand to fall on the priests of the LORD.
units.rightText: Then the king ordered the guards at his side, “Turn and kill the priests of the LORD, because they too sided with David. For they knew he was fleeing, but they did not tell me.”

units.leftText: The king said to Doeg, “Turn and attack the priests!”
units.rightText: So the king ordered Doeg, “You turn and strike down the priests!”

units.leftText: He struck Nob, the city of the priests, with the edge of the sword—both men and women, children and nursing babies, and cattle, donkeys, and sheep, with the edge of the sword.
units.rightText: He also put to the sword Nob, the city of the priests, with its men and women, children and infants, oxen, donkeys, and sheep.

units.leftText: One of the sons of Ahimelech the son of Ahitub, named Abiathar, escaped and fled after David.
units.rightText: But one of the sons of Ahimelech son of Ahitub escaped. His name was Abiathar, and he fled to David.

units.leftText: Abiathar told David that Saul had slain the LORD’s priests.
units.rightText: And Abiathar told David that Saul had killed the priests of the LORD.

units.leftText: David said to Abiathar, “I knew on that day, when Doeg the Edomite was there, that he would surely tell Saul. I am responsible for the death of all the persons of your father’s house.
units.rightText: Then David said to Abiathar, “I knew that Doeg the Edomite was there that day, and that he was sure to tell Saul. I myself am responsible for the lives of everyone in your father’s house.

units.leftText: Stay with me. Don’t be afraid, for he who seeks my life seeks your life. You will be safe with me.”
units.rightText: Stay with me; do not be afraid, for he who seeks your life is seeking mine as well. You will be safe with me.”

units.leftText: David was told, “Behold, the Philistines are fighting against Keilah, and are robbing the threshing floors.”
units.rightText: Now it was reported to David, “Look, the Philistines are fighting against Keilah and looting the threshing floors.”

units.leftText: Therefore David inquired of the LORD, saying, “Shall I go and strike these Philistines?”
units.rightText: So David inquired of the LORD, “Should I go and attack these Philistines?”

units.leftText: David’s men said to him, “Behold, we are afraid here in Judah. How much more then if we go to Keilah against the armies of the Philistines?”
units.rightText: But David’s men said to him, “Look, we are afraid here in Judah; how much more if we go to Keilah against the armies of the Philistines?”

units.leftText: Then David inquired of the LORD yet again. The LORD answered him, and said, “Arise, go down to Keilah; for I will deliver the Philistines into your hand.”
units.rightText: Once again, David inquired of the LORD, and the LORD answered him: “Go at once to Keilah, for I will deliver the Philistines into your hand.”

units.leftText: David and his men went to Keilah and fought with the Philistines, and brought away their livestock, and killed them with a great slaughter. So David saved the inhabitants of Keilah.
units.rightText: Then David and his men went to Keilah, fought against the Philistines, and carried off their livestock, striking them with a mighty blow. So David saved the people of Keilah.

units.leftText: When Abiathar the son of Ahimelech fled to David to Keilah, he came down with an ephod in his hand.
units.rightText: (Now Abiathar son of Ahimelech had brought the ephod with him when he fled to David at Keilah.)

units.leftText: Saul was told that David had come to Keilah. Saul said, “God has delivered him into my hand, for he is shut in by entering into a town that has gates and bars.”
units.rightText: When Saul was told that David had gone to Keilah, he said, “God has delivered him into my hand, for he has trapped himself by entering a town with gates and bars.”

units.leftText: Saul summoned all the people to war, to go down to Keilah to besiege David and his men.
units.rightText: Then Saul summoned all his troops to go to war at Keilah and besiege David and his men.

units.leftText: David knew that Saul was devising mischief against him. He said to Abiathar the priest, “Bring the ephod here.”
units.rightText: When David learned that Saul was plotting evil against him, he said to Abiathar the priest, “Bring the ephod.”

units.leftText: Then David said, “O LORD, the God of Israel, your servant has surely heard that Saul seeks to come to Keilah to destroy the city for my sake.
units.rightText: And David said, “O LORD, God of Israel, Your servant has heard that Saul intends to come to Keilah and destroy the city on my account.

units.leftText: Will the men of Keilah deliver me up into his hand? Will Saul come down, as your servant has heard? LORD, the God of Israel, I beg you, tell your servant.”
units.rightText: Will the citizens of Keilah surrender me into his hand? Will Saul come down, as Your servant has heard? O LORD, God of Israel, please tell Your servant.”
rightNotes: 23:11 Some manuscripts omit this question.

units.leftText: Then David said, “Will the men of Keilah deliver me and my men into the hand of Saul?”
units.rightText: So David asked, “Will the citizens of Keilah surrender me and my men into the hand of Saul?”

units.leftText: Then David and his men, who were about six hundred, arose and departed out of Keilah and went wherever they could go. Saul was told that David had escaped from Keilah; and he gave up going there.
units.rightText: Then David and his men, about six hundred strong, set out and departed from Keilah, moving from place to place. When Saul was told that David had escaped from Keilah, he declined to go forth.

units.leftText: David stayed in the wilderness in the strongholds, and remained in the hill country in the wilderness of Ziph. Saul sought him every day, but God didn’t deliver him into his hand.
units.rightText: And David stayed in the wilderness strongholds and in the hill country of the Wilderness of Ziph. Day after day Saul searched for him, but God would not deliver David into his hand.

units.leftText: David saw that Saul had come out to seek his life. David was in the wilderness of Ziph in the woods.
units.rightText: While David was in Horesh in the Wilderness of Ziph, he saw that Saul had come out to take his life.

units.leftText: Jonathan, Saul’s son, arose and went to David into the woods, and strengthened his hand in God.
units.rightText: And Saul’s son Jonathan came to David in Horesh and strengthened his hand in God,

units.leftText: He said to him, “Don’t be afraid, for the hand of Saul my father won’t find you; and you will be king over Israel, and I will be next to you; and Saul my father knows that also.”
units.rightText: saying, “Do not be afraid, for my father Saul will never lay a hand on you. And you will be king over Israel, and I will be your second-in-command. Even my father Saul knows this is true.”

units.leftText: They both made a covenant before the LORD. Then David stayed in the woods and Jonathan went to his house.
units.rightText: So the two of them made a covenant before the LORD. And David remained in Horesh, while Jonathan went home.

units.leftText: Then the Ziphites came up to Saul to Gibeah, saying, “Doesn’t David hide himself with us in the strongholds in the woods, in the hill of Hachilah, which is on the south of the desert?
units.rightText: Then the Ziphites came up to Saul at Gibeah and said, “Is not David hiding among us in the strongholds at Horesh, on the hill of Hachilah south of Jeshimon?

units.leftText: Now therefore, O king, come down. According to all the desire of your soul to come down; and our part will be to deliver him up into the king’s hand.”
units.rightText: Now, O king, come down whenever your soul desires, and we will be responsible for delivering him into your hand.”

units.leftText: Saul said, “You are blessed by the LORD, for you have had compassion on me.
units.rightText: “May you be blessed by the LORD,” replied Saul, “for you have had compassion on me.

units.leftText: Please go make yet more sure, and know and see his place where his haunt is, and who has seen him there; for I have been told that he is very cunning.
units.rightText: Please go and prepare further. Investigate and watch carefully where he goes and who has seen him there, for I am told that he is extremely cunning.

units.leftText: See therefore, and take knowledge of all the lurking places where he hides himself; and come again to me with certainty, and I will go with you. It shall happen, if he is in the land, that I will search him out among all the thousands of Judah.”
units.rightText: Observe and find out all the places where he hides. Then come back to me with certainty, and I will go with you. If he is in the land, I will search him out among all the clans of Judah.”

units.leftText: They arose, and went to Ziph before Saul; but David and his men were in the wilderness of Maon, in the Arabah on the south of the desert.
units.rightText: So they set out and went to Ziph ahead of Saul. Now David and his men were in the Wilderness of Maon in the Arabah south of Jeshimon,

units.leftText: Saul and his men went to seek him. When David was told, he went down to the rock, and stayed in the wilderness of Maon. When Saul heard that, he pursued David in the wilderness of Maon.
units.rightText: and Saul and his men went to seek him. When David was told about it, he went down to the rock and stayed in the Wilderness of Maon. And when Saul heard of this, he pursued David there.

units.leftText: Saul went on this side of the mountain, and David and his men on that side of the mountain; and David hurried to get away for fear of Saul, for Saul and his men surrounded David and his men to take them.
units.rightText: Saul was proceeding along one side of the mountain, and David and his men along the other side. Even though David was hurrying to get away, Saul and his men were closing in on David and his men to capture them.

units.leftText: But a messenger came to Saul, saying, “Hurry and come, for the Philistines have made a raid on the land!”
units.rightText: Then a messenger came to Saul, saying, “Come quickly, for the Philistines have raided the land!”

units.leftText: So Saul returned from pursuing David, and went against the Philistines. Therefore they called that place Sela Hammahlekoth.
units.rightText: So Saul broke off his pursuit of David and went to meet the Philistines. That is why that place is called Sela-hammahlekoth.
leftNotes: 23:28 “Sela Hammahlekoth” means “rock of parting”.
rightNotes: 23:28 Sela-hammahlekoth means Rock of Escape.

units.leftText: David went up from there and lived in the strongholds of En Gedi.
units.rightText: And David went up from there and lived in the strongholds of En-gedi.

units.leftText: When Saul had returned from following the Philistines, he was told, “Behold, David is in the wilderness of En Gedi.”
units.rightText: After Saul had returned from pursuing the Philistines, he was told, “David is in the wilderness of En-gedi.”

units.leftText: Then Saul took three thousand chosen men out of all Israel, and went to seek David and his men on the rocks of the wild goats.
units.rightText: So Saul took three thousand chosen men from all Israel and went to look for David and his men in the region of the Rocks of the Wild Goats.

units.leftText: He came to the sheep pens by the way, where there was a cave; and Saul went in to relieve himself. Now David and his men were staying in the innermost parts of the cave.
units.rightText: Soon Saul came to the sheepfolds along the road, where there was a cave, and he went in to relieve himself. And David and his men were hiding in the recesses of the cave.
rightNotes: 24:3 Literally cover his feet, a euphemism for relieving oneself

units.leftText: David’s men said to him, “Behold, the day of which the LORD said to you, ‘Behold, I will deliver your enemy into your hand, and you shall do to him as it shall seem good to you.’” Then David arose and cut off the skirt of Saul’s robe secretly.
units.rightText: So David’s men said to him, “This is the day about which the LORD said to you, ‘Behold, I will deliver your enemy into your hand, that you may do with him as you wish.’”

units.leftText: Afterward, David’s heart struck him because he had cut off Saul’s skirt.
units.rightText: Afterward, David’s conscience was stricken because he had cut off the corner of Saul’s robe.

units.leftText: He said to his men, “The LORD forbid that I should do this thing to my lord, the LORD’s anointed, to stretch out my hand against him, since he is the LORD’s anointed.”
units.rightText: So he said to his men, “The LORD forbid that I should do such a thing to my master, the LORD’s anointed. May I never lift my hand against him, since he is the LORD’s anointed.”

units.leftText: So David checked his men with these words, and didn’t allow them to rise against Saul. Saul rose up out of the cave, and went on his way.
units.rightText: With these words David restrained his men, and he did not let them rise up against Saul. Then Saul left the cave and went on his way.

units.leftText: David also arose afterward, and went out of the cave and cried after Saul, saying, “My lord the king!”
units.rightText: After that, David got up, went out of the cave, and called out to Saul, “My lord the king!”

units.leftText: David said to Saul, “Why do you listen to men’s words, saying, ‘Behold, David seeks to harm you’?
units.rightText: and said to Saul, “Why do you listen to the words of men who say, ‘Look, David intends to harm you’ ?

units.leftText: Behold, today your eyes have seen how the LORD had delivered you today into my hand in the cave. Some urged me to kill you, but I spared you. I said, ‘I will not stretch out my hand against my lord, for he is the LORD’s anointed.’
units.rightText: Behold, this day you have seen with your own eyes that the LORD delivered you into my hand in the cave. I was told to kill you, but I spared you and said, ‘I will not lift my hand against my lord, since he is the LORD’s anointed.’

units.leftText: Moreover, my father, behold, yes, see the skirt of your robe in my hand; for in that I cut off the skirt of your robe and didn’t kill you, know and see that there is neither evil nor disobedience in my hand. I have not sinned against you, though you hunt for my life to take it.
units.rightText: See, my father, look at the corner of your robe in my hand. For I cut it off, but I did not kill you. Know and see that there is no evil or rebellion in my hands. I have not sinned against you, even though you are hunting me down to take my life.

units.leftText: May the LORD judge between me and you, and may the LORD avenge me of you; but my hand will not be on you.
units.rightText: May the LORD judge between you and me, and may the LORD take vengeance on you, but my hand will never be against you.

units.leftText: As the proverb of the ancients says, ‘Out of the wicked comes wickedness;’ but my hand will not be on you.
units.rightText: As the old proverb says, ‘Wickedness proceeds from the wicked.’ But my hand will never be against you.

units.leftText: Against whom has the king of Israel come out? Whom do you pursue? A dead dog? A flea?
units.rightText: Against whom has the king of Israel come out? Whom are you pursuing? A dead dog? A flea?

units.leftText: May the LORD therefore be judge, and give sentence between me and you, and see, and plead my cause, and deliver me out of your hand.”
units.rightText: May the LORD be our judge and decide between you and me. May He take notice and plead my case and deliver me from your hand.”

units.leftText: It came to pass, when David had finished speaking these words to Saul, that Saul said, “Is that your voice, my son David?” Saul lifted up his voice and wept.
units.rightText: When David had finished saying these things, Saul called back, “Is that your voice, David my son?”

units.leftText: He said to David, “You are more righteous than I; for you have done good to me, whereas I have done evil to you.
units.rightText: and said to David, “You are more righteous than I, for you have rewarded me with good, though I have rewarded you with evil.

units.leftText: You have declared today how you have dealt well with me, because when the LORD had delivered me up into your hand, you didn’t kill me.
units.rightText: And you have declared this day how you have treated me well, for when the LORD delivered me into your hand, you did not kill me.

units.leftText: For if a man finds his enemy, will he let him go away unharmed? Therefore may the LORD reward you good for that which you have done to me today.
units.rightText: When a man finds his enemy, does he let him go away unharmed? May the LORD reward you with good for what you have done for me this day.

units.leftText: Now, behold, I know that you will surely be king, and that the kingdom of Israel will be established in your hand.
units.rightText: Now I know for sure that you will be king and that the kingdom of Israel will be established in your hands.

units.leftText: Swear now therefore to me by the LORD that you will not cut off my offspring after me, and that you will not destroy my name out of my father’s house.”
units.rightText: So now, swear to me by the LORD that you will not cut off my descendants or wipe out my name from my father’s house.”

units.leftText: David swore to Saul. Saul went home, but David and his men went up to the stronghold.
units.rightText: So David gave his oath to Saul. Then Saul returned home, but David and his men went up to the stronghold.

units.leftText: Samuel died; and all Israel gathered themselves together and mourned for him, and buried him at his house at Ramah.
units.rightText: When Samuel died, all Israel gathered to mourn for him; and they buried him at his home in Ramah.

units.leftText: There was a man in Maon whose possessions were in Carmel; and the man was very great. He had three thousand sheep and a thousand goats; and he was shearing his sheep in Carmel.
units.rightText: Now there was a man in Maon whose business was in Carmel. He was a very wealthy man with a thousand goats and three thousand sheep, which he was shearing in Carmel.

units.leftText: Now the name of the man was Nabal; and the name of his wife Abigail. This woman was intelligent and had a beautiful face; but the man was surly and evil in his doings. He was of the house of Caleb.
units.rightText: His name was Nabal, and his wife’s name was Abigail. She was an intelligent and beautiful woman, but her husband, a Calebite, was harsh and evil in his dealings.

units.leftText: David heard in the wilderness that Nabal was shearing his sheep.
units.rightText: While David was in the wilderness, he heard that Nabal was shearing sheep.

units.leftText: David sent ten young men; and David said to the young men, “Go up to Carmel, and go to Nabal, and greet him in my name.
units.rightText: So David sent ten young men and instructed them, “Go up to Nabal at Carmel. Greet him in my name

units.leftText: Tell him, ‘Long life to you! Peace be to you! Peace be to your house! Peace be to all that you have!
units.rightText: and say to him, ‘Long life to you, and peace to you and to your house and to all that belongs to you.

units.leftText: Now I have heard that you have shearers. Your shepherds have now been with us, and we didn’t harm them. Nothing was missing from them all the time they were in Carmel.
units.rightText: Now I hear that it is time for shearing. When your shepherds were with us, we did not harass them, and nothing of theirs was missing the whole time they were in Carmel.

units.leftText: Ask your young men, and they will tell you. Therefore let the young men find favor in your eyes, for we come on a good day. Please give whatever comes to your hand to your servants and to your son David.’”
units.rightText: Ask your young men, and they will tell you. So let my young men find favor with you, for we have come on the day of a feast. Please give whatever you can spare to your servants and to your son David.’”

units.leftText: When David’s young men came, they spoke to Nabal all those words in the name of David, and waited.
units.rightText: When David’s young men arrived, they relayed all these words to Nabal on behalf of David. Then they waited.

units.leftText: Nabal answered David’s servants and said, “Who is David? Who is the son of Jesse? There are many servants who break away from their masters these days.
units.rightText: But Nabal asked them, “Who is David? Who is this son of Jesse? Many servants these days are breaking away from their masters.

units.leftText: Shall I then take my bread, my water, and my meat that I have killed for my shearers, and give it to men who I don’t know where they come from?”
units.rightText: Why should I take my bread and water and the meat I have slaughtered for my shearers, and give them to these men whose origin I do not know?”

units.leftText: So David’s young men turned on their way and went back, and came and told him all these words.
units.rightText: So David’s men turned around and went back, and they relayed to him all these words.

units.leftText: David said to his men, “Every man put on his sword!”
units.rightText: And David said to his men, “Strap on your swords!” So David and all his men strapped on their swords, and about four hundred men followed David, while two hundred stayed with the supplies.

units.leftText: But one of the young men told Abigail, Nabal’s wife, saying, “Behold, David sent messengers out of the wilderness to greet our master; and he insulted them.
units.rightText: Meanwhile, one of Nabal’s young men informed Nabal’s wife Abigail, “Look, David sent messengers from the wilderness to greet our master, but he screamed at them.

units.leftText: But the men were very good to us, and we were not harmed, and we didn’t miss anything as long as we went with them, when we were in the fields.
units.rightText: Yet these men were very good to us. When we were in the field, we were not harassed, and nothing of ours went missing the whole time we lived among them.

units.leftText: They were a wall to us both by night and by day, all the while we were with them keeping the sheep.
units.rightText: They were a wall around us, both day and night, the whole time we were herding our sheep near them.

units.leftText: Now therefore know and consider what you will do; for evil is determined against our master and against all his house, for he is such a worthless fellow that one can’t speak to him.”
units.rightText: Now consider carefully what you must do, because disaster looms over our master and all his household. For he is such a scoundrel that nobody can speak to him!”

units.leftText: Then Abigail hurried and took two hundred loaves of bread, two containers of wine, five sheep ready dressed, five seahs of parched grain, one hundred clusters of raisins, and two hundred cakes of figs, and laid them on donkeys.
units.rightText: Then Abigail hurried and took two hundred loaves of bread, two skins of wine, five butchered sheep, five seahs of roasted grain, a hundred clusters of raisins, and two hundred cakes of figs. She loaded them on donkeys

rightNotes: 25:18 5 seahs is approximately 33 dry quarts or 36.5 liters of roasted grain.

units.leftText: She said to her young men, “Go on before me. Behold, I am coming after you.” But she didn’t tell her husband, Nabal.
units.rightText: and said to her young men, “Go ahead of me. I will be right behind you.” But she did not tell her husband Nabal.

units.leftText: As she rode on her donkey, and came down hidden by the mountain, behold, David and his men came down toward her, and she met them.
units.rightText: As Abigail came riding her donkey into a mountain ravine, she saw David and his men coming down toward her, and she met them.

units.leftText: Now David had said, “Surely in vain I have kept all that this fellow has in the wilderness, so that nothing was missed of all that pertained to him. He has returned me evil for good.
units.rightText: Now David had just said, “In vain I have protected all that belonged to this man in the wilderness. Nothing that belongs to him has gone missing, yet he has paid me back evil for good.

units.leftText: God do so to the enemies of David, and more also, if I leave of all that belongs to him by the morning light so much as one who urinates on a wall.”
units.rightText: May God punish David, and ever so severely, if I let one male belonging to Nabal survive until morning.”
leftNotes: 25:22 or, male.

units.leftText: When Abigail saw David, she hurried and got off her donkey, and fell before David on her face and bowed herself to the ground.
units.rightText: When Abigail saw David, she quickly got off the donkey, fell facedown, and bowed before him.

units.leftText: She fell at his feet and said, “On me, my lord, on me be the blame! Please let your servant speak in your ears. Hear the words of your servant.
units.rightText: She fell at his feet and said, “My lord, may the blame be on me alone, but please let your servant speak to you; hear the words of your servant.

units.leftText: Please don’t let my lord pay attention to this worthless fellow, Nabal, for as his name is, so is he. Nabal is his name, and folly is with him; but I, your servant, didn’t see my lord’s young men whom you sent.
units.rightText: My lord should pay no attention to this scoundrel Nabal, for he lives up to his name: His name means Fool, and folly accompanies him. I, your servant, did not see my lord’s young men whom you sent.
leftNotes: 25:25 “Nabal” means “foolish”.
rightNotes: 25:25 Nabal means fool.

units.leftText: Now therefore, my lord, as the LORD lives and as your soul lives, since the LORD has withheld you from blood guiltiness and from avenging yourself with your own hand, now therefore let your enemies and those who seek evil to my lord be as Nabal.
units.rightText: Now, my lord, as surely as the LORD lives and you yourself live, since the LORD has held you back from bloodshed and from avenging yourself with your own hand, may your enemies and those who seek harm for my lord be like Nabal.

units.leftText: Now this present which your servant has brought to my lord, let it be given to the young men who follow my lord.
units.rightText: Now let this gift your servant has brought to my lord be given to the young men who follow you.

units.leftText: Please forgive the trespass of your servant. For the LORD will certainly make my lord a sure house, because my lord fights the LORD’s battles. Evil will not be found in you all your days.
units.rightText: Please forgive your servant’s offense, for the LORD will surely make a lasting dynasty for my lord, because he fights the LORD’s battles. May no evil be found in you as long as you live.

units.leftText: Though men may rise up to pursue you and to seek your soul, yet the soul of my lord will be bound in the bundle of life with the LORD your God. He will sling out the souls of your enemies as from a sling’s pocket.
units.rightText: And should someone pursue you and seek your life, then the life of my lord will be bound securely by the LORD your God in the bundle of the living. But He shall fling away the lives of your enemies like stones from a sling.
rightNotes: 25:29 Literally fling away the souls of your enemies as from the pocket of a sling

units.leftText: It will come to pass, when the LORD has done to my lord according to all the good that he has spoken concerning you, and has appointed you prince over Israel,
units.rightText: When the LORD has done for my lord all the good He promised, and when He has appointed you ruler over Israel,

units.leftText: that this shall be no grief to you, nor offense of heart to my lord, either that you have shed blood without cause, or that my lord has avenged himself. When the LORD has dealt well with my lord, then remember your servant.”
units.rightText: then my lord will have no remorse or guilt of conscience over needless bloodshed and revenge. And when the LORD has dealt well with my lord, may you remember your servant.”

units.leftText: David said to Abigail, “Blessed is the LORD, the God of Israel, who sent you today to meet me!
units.rightText: Then David said to Abigail, “Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who sent you to meet me this day!

units.leftText: Blessed is your discretion, and blessed are you, who have kept me today from blood guiltiness, and from avenging myself with my own hand.
units.rightText: Blessed is your discernment, and blessed are you, because today you kept me from bloodshed and from avenging myself by my own hand.

units.leftText: For indeed, as the LORD the God of Israel lives, who has withheld me from harming you, unless you had hurried and come to meet me, surely there wouldn’t have been left to Nabal by the morning light so much as one who urinates on a wall.”
units.rightText: Otherwise, as surely as the LORD, the God of Israel, lives, who has restrained me from harming you, if you had not come quickly to meet me, then surely no male belonging to Nabal would have been left alive by morning light.”
leftNotes: 25:34 or, one male.

units.leftText: So David received from her hand that which she had brought him. Then he said to her, “Go up in peace to your house. Behold, I have listened to your voice and have granted your request.”
units.rightText: Then David accepted from her hand what she had brought him, and he said to her, “Go home in peace. See, I have heeded your voice and granted your request.”

units.leftText: Abigail came to Nabal; and behold, he held a feast in his house like the feast of a king. Nabal’s heart was merry within him, for he was very drunk. Therefore she told him nothing until the morning light.
units.rightText: When Abigail returned to Nabal, there he was in the house, holding a feast fit for a king, in high spirits and very drunk. So she told him nothing until morning light.

units.leftText: In the morning, when the wine had gone out of Nabal, his wife told him these things; and his heart died within him, and he became as a stone.
units.rightText: In the morning when Nabal was sober, his wife told him about these events, and his heart failed within him, and he became like a stone.

units.leftText: About ten days later, the LORD struck Nabal, so that he died.
units.rightText: About ten days later, the LORD struck Nabal dead.

units.leftText: When David heard that Nabal was dead, he said, “Blessed is the LORD, who has pleaded the cause of my reproach from the hand of Nabal, and has kept back his servant from evil. The LORD has returned the evildoing of Nabal on his own head.”
units.rightText: On hearing that Nabal was dead, David said, “Blessed be the LORD, who has upheld my cause against the reproach of Nabal and has restrained His servant from evil. For the LORD has brought the wickedness of Nabal down upon his own head.”

units.leftText: When David’s servants had come to Abigail to Carmel, they spoke to her, saying, “David has sent us to you, to take you to him as wife.”
units.rightText: When his servants came to Abigail at Carmel, they said, “David has sent us to take you as his wife.”

units.leftText: She arose and bowed herself with her face to the earth, and said, “Behold, your servant is a servant to wash the feet of the servants of my lord.”
units.rightText: She arose, bowed facedown, and said, “Here is your servant, ready to serve and to wash the feet of my lord’s servants.”

units.leftText: Abigail hurriedly arose and rode on a donkey with her five maids who followed her; and she went after the messengers of David, and became his wife.
units.rightText: So Abigail hurried and got on a donkey, and attended by five of her maidens, she followed David’s messengers and became his wife.

units.leftText: David also took Ahinoam of Jezreel; and they both became his wives.
units.rightText: David had also married Ahinoam of Jezreel. So she and Abigail were both his wives.

units.leftText: Now Saul had given Michal his daughter, David’s wife, to Palti the son of Laish, who was of Gallim.
units.rightText: But Saul had given his daughter Michal, David’s wife, to Palti son of Laish, who was from Gallim.

units.leftText: The Ziphites came to Saul to Gibeah, saying, “Doesn’t David hide himself in the hill of Hachilah, which is before the desert?”
units.rightText: Then the Ziphites came to Saul at Gibeah and said, “Is not David hiding on the hill of Hachilah, opposite Jeshimon?”

units.leftText: Then Saul arose and went down to the wilderness of Ziph, having three thousand chosen men of Israel with him, to seek David in the wilderness of Ziph.
units.rightText: So Saul, accompanied by three thousand chosen men of Israel, went down to the Wilderness of Ziph to search for David there.

units.leftText: Saul encamped in the hill of Hachilah, which is before the desert, by the way. But David stayed in the wilderness, and he saw that Saul came after him into the wilderness.

units.rightText: David sent out spies to verify that Saul had arrived.

units.leftText: Then David arose and came to the place where Saul had encamped; and David saw the place where Saul lay, with Abner the son of Ner, the captain of his army. Saul lay within the place of the wagons, and the people were encamped around him.
units.rightText: Then David set out and went to the place where Saul had camped. He saw the place where Saul and Abner son of Ner, the general of his army, had lain down. Saul was lying inside the inner circle of the camp, with the troops camped around him.

units.leftText: Then David answered and said to Ahimelech the Hittite, and to Abishai the son of Zeruiah, brother of Joab, saying, “Who will go down with me to Saul to the camp?”
units.rightText: And David asked Ahimelech the Hittite and Abishai son of Zeruiah, Joab’s brother, “Who will go down with me to Saul in the camp?”

units.leftText: So David and Abishai came to the people by night; and, behold, Saul lay sleeping within the place of the wagons, with his spear stuck in the ground at his head; and Abner and the people lay around him.
units.rightText: That night David and Abishai came to the troops, and Saul was lying there asleep in the inner circle of the camp, with his spear stuck in the ground by his head. And Abner and the troops were lying around him.

units.leftText: Then Abishai said to David, “God has delivered up your enemy into your hand today. Now therefore please let me strike him with the spear to the earth at one stroke, and I will not strike him the second time.”
units.rightText: Abishai said to David, “Today God has delivered your enemy into your hand. Now, therefore, please let me thrust the spear through him into the ground with one stroke. I will not need to strike him twice!”

units.leftText: David said to Abishai, “Don’t destroy him, for who can stretch out his hand against the LORD’s anointed, and be guiltless?”
units.rightText: But David said to Abishai, “Do not destroy him, for who can extend a hand against the LORD’s anointed and be guiltless?”

units.leftText: David said, “As the LORD lives, the LORD will strike him; or his day shall come to die, or he shall go down into battle and perish.
units.rightText: David added, “As surely as the LORD lives, the LORD Himself will strike him down; either his day will come and he will die, or he will go into battle and perish.

units.leftText: The LORD forbid that I should stretch out my hand against the LORD’s anointed; but now please take the spear that is at his head and the jar of water, and let’s go.”
units.rightText: But the LORD forbid that I should extend my hand against the LORD’s anointed. Instead, take the spear and water jug by his head, and let us go.”

units.leftText: So David took the spear and the jar of water from Saul’s head, and they went away. No man saw it, or knew it, nor did any awake; for they were all asleep, because a deep sleep from the LORD had fallen on them.
units.rightText: So David took the spear and water jug by Saul’s head, and they departed. No one saw them or knew about it, nor did anyone wake up; they all remained asleep, because a deep sleep from the LORD had fallen on them.

units.leftText: Then David went over to the other side, and stood on the top of the mountain far away, a great space being between them;
units.rightText: Then David crossed to the other side and stood atop the mountain at a distance; there was a wide gulf between them.

units.leftText: and David cried to the people, and to Abner the son of Ner, saying, “Don’t you answer, Abner?”
units.rightText: And David shouted to the troops and to Abner son of Ner, “Will you not answer me, Abner?”

units.leftText: David said to Abner, “Aren’t you a man? Who is like you in Israel? Why then have you not kept watch over your lord the king? For one of the people came in to destroy your lord the king.
units.rightText: So David said to Abner, “You are a man, aren’t you? And who in Israel is your equal? Why then did you not protect your lord the king when one of the people came to destroy him?

units.leftText: This thing isn’t good that you have done. As the LORD lives, you are worthy to die, because you have not kept watch over your lord, the LORD’s anointed. Now see where the king’s spear is, and the jar of water that was at his head.”
units.rightText: This thing you have done is not good. As surely as the LORD lives, all of you deserve to die, since you did not protect your lord, the LORD’s anointed. Now look around. Where are the king’s spear and water jug that were by his head?”

units.leftText: Saul recognized David’s voice, and said, “Is this your voice, my son David?”
units.rightText: Then Saul recognized David’s voice and asked, “Is that your voice, David my son?”

units.leftText: He said, “Why does my lord pursue his servant? For what have I done? What evil is in my hand?
units.rightText: And he continued, “Why is my lord pursuing his servant? What have I done? What evil is in my hand?

units.leftText: Now therefore, please let my lord the king hear the words of his servant. If it is so that the LORD has stirred you up against me, let him accept an offering. But if it is the children of men, they are cursed before the LORD; for they have driven me out today that I shouldn’t cling to the LORD’s inheritance, saying, ‘Go, serve other gods!’
units.rightText: Now please, may my lord the king hear the words of his servant: If the LORD has stirred you up against me, then may He accept an offering. But if men have done it, may they be cursed in the presence of the LORD! For today they have driven me away from sharing in the inheritance of the LORD, saying, ‘Go, serve other gods.’

units.leftText: Now therefore, don’t let my blood fall to the earth away from the presence of the LORD; for the king of Israel has come out to seek a flea, as when one hunts a partridge in the mountains.”
units.rightText: So do not let my blood fall to the ground far from the presence of the LORD. For the king of Israel has come out to look for a flea, like one who hunts a partridge in the mountains.”

units.leftText: Then Saul said, “I have sinned. Return, my son David; for I will no more do you harm, because my life was precious in your eyes today. Behold, I have played the fool, and have erred exceedingly.”
units.rightText: Then Saul replied, “I have sinned. Come back, David my son. I will never harm you again, because today you considered my life precious. I have played the fool and have committed a grave error!”

units.leftText: David answered, “Behold the spear, O king! Let one of the young men come over and get it.
units.rightText: “Here is the king’s spear,” David answered. “Let one of the young men come over and get it.

units.leftText: The LORD will give to every man his righteousness and his faithfulness; because the LORD delivered you into my hand today, and I wouldn’t stretch out my hand against the LORD’s anointed.
units.rightText: May the LORD repay every man for his righteousness and faithfulness. For the LORD delivered you into my hand today, but I would not extend my hand against the LORD’s anointed.

units.leftText: Behold, as your life was respected today in my eyes, so let my life be respected in the LORD’s eyes, and let him deliver me out of all oppression.”
units.rightText: As surely as I valued your life today, so may the LORD value my life and rescue me from all trouble.”

units.leftText: Then Saul said to David, “You are blessed, my son David. You will both do mightily, and will surely prevail.”
units.rightText: Saul said to him, “May you be blessed, David my son. You will accomplish great things and will surely prevail.”

units.leftText: David said in his heart, “I will now perish one day by the hand of Saul. There is nothing better for me than that I should escape into the land of the Philistines; and Saul will despair of me, to seek me any more in all the borders of Israel. So I will escape out of his hand.”
units.rightText: David, however, said to himself, “One of these days now I will be swept away by the hand of Saul. There is nothing better for me than to escape to the land of the Philistines. Then Saul will stop searching for me all over Israel, and I will slip out of his hand.”

units.leftText: David arose and passed over, he and the six hundred men who were with him, to Achish the son of Maoch, king of Gath.
units.rightText: So David set out with his six hundred men and went to Achish son of Maoch, the king of Gath.
rightNotes: 27:2 Maoch is a variant of Maacah; see 1 Kings 2:39|1KI 2:39*.

units.leftText: David lived with Achish at Gath, he and his men, every man with his household, even David with his two wives, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess and Abigail the Carmelitess, Nabal’s wife.
units.rightText: David and his men settled in Gath with Achish. Each man had his family with him, and David had his two wives: Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail of Carmel, the widow of Nabal.

units.leftText: Saul was told that David had fled to Gath, so he stopped looking for him.
units.rightText: And when Saul learned that David had fled to Gath, he no longer searched for him.

units.leftText: David said to Achish, “If now I have found favor in your eyes, let them give me a place in one of the cities in the country, that I may dwell there. For why should your servant dwell in the royal city with you?”
units.rightText: Then David said to Achish, “If I have found favor in your eyes, let me be assigned a place in one of the outlying towns, so I can live there. For why should your servant live in the royal city with you?”

units.leftText: Then Achish gave him Ziklag that day: therefore Ziklag belongs to the kings of Judah to this day.
units.rightText: That day Achish gave him Ziklag, and to this day it still belongs to the kings of Judah.

units.leftText: The number of the days that David lived in the country of the Philistines was a full year and four months.
units.rightText: And the time that David lived in Philistine territory amounted to a year and four months.

units.leftText: David and his men went up and raided the Geshurites, the Girzites, and the Amalekites; for those were the inhabitants of the land who were of old, on the way to Shur, even to the land of Egypt.
units.rightText: Now David and his men went up and raided the Geshurites, the Girzites, and the Amalekites. (From ancient times these people had inhabited the land extending to Shur and Egypt.)

units.leftText: David struck the land, and saved no man or woman alive, and took away the sheep, the cattle, the donkeys, the camels, and the clothing. Then he returned, and came to Achish.
units.rightText: Whenever David attacked a territory, he did not leave a man or woman alive, but he took the flocks and herds, the donkeys, camels, and clothing.

units.leftText: Achish said, “Against whom have you made a raid today?”
units.rightText: who would ask him, “What have you raided today?”

units.leftText: David saved neither man nor woman alive to bring them to Gath, saying, “Lest they should tell about us, saying, ‘David did this, and this has been his way all the time he has lived in the country of the Philistines.’”
units.rightText: David did not leave a man or woman alive to be brought to Gath, for he said, “Otherwise they will report us, saying, ‘This is what David did.’” And this was David’s custom the whole time he lived in Philistine territory.

units.leftText: Achish believed David, saying, “He has made his people Israel utterly to abhor him. Therefore he will be my servant forever.”
units.rightText: So Achish trusted David, thinking, “Since he has made himself an utter stench to his people Israel, he will be my servant forever.”

units.leftText: In those days, the Philistines gathered their armies together for warfare, to fight with Israel. Achish said to David, “Know assuredly that you will go out with me in the army, you and your men.”
units.rightText: Now in those days the Philistines gathered their forces for warfare against Israel. So Achish said to David, “You must understand that you and your men are to go out to battle with me.”

units.leftText: David said to Achish, “Therefore you will know what your servant can do.”
units.rightText: David replied, “Then you will come to know what your servant can do.”

units.leftText: Now Samuel was dead, and all Israel had mourned for him and buried him in Ramah, even in his own city. Saul had sent away those who had familiar spirits and the wizards out of the land.
units.rightText: Now by this time Samuel had died, and all Israel had mourned for him and buried him in Ramah, his own city. And Saul had removed the mediums and spiritists from the land.

units.leftText: The Philistines gathered themselves together, and came and encamped in Shunem; and Saul gathered all Israel together, and they encamped in Gilboa.
units.rightText: The Philistines gathered together and camped at Shunem, while Saul gathered all Israel and camped at Gilboa.

units.leftText: When Saul saw the army of the Philistines, he was afraid, and his heart trembled greatly.
units.rightText: When Saul saw the Philistine army, he was afraid and trembled violently.

units.leftText: When Saul inquired of the LORD, the LORD didn’t answer him by dreams, by Urim, or by prophets.
units.rightText: He inquired of the LORD, but the LORD did not answer him by dreams or Urim or prophets.

units.leftText: Then Saul said to his servants, “Seek for me a woman who has a familiar spirit, that I may go to her and inquire of her.”
units.rightText: Then Saul said to his servants, “Find me a woman who is a medium, so I can go and consult her.”

units.leftText: Saul disguised himself and put on other clothing, and went, he and two men with him, and they came to the woman by night. Then he said, “Please consult for me by the familiar spirit, and bring me up whomever I shall name to you.”
units.rightText: So Saul disguised himself by putting on different clothes, and he set out with two of his men. They came to the woman at night, and Saul said, “Consult a spirit for me. Bring up for me the one I name.”

units.leftText: The woman said to him, “Behold, you know what Saul has done, how he has cut off those who have familiar spirits and the wizards out of the land. Why then do you lay a snare for my life, to cause me to die?”
units.rightText: But the woman replied, “Surely you know what Saul has done, how he has killed the mediums and spiritists in the land. Why have you set a trap to get me killed?”

units.leftText: Saul swore to her by the LORD, saying, “As the LORD lives, no punishment will happen to you for this thing.”
units.rightText: Then Saul swore to her by the LORD: “As surely as the LORD lives, no punishment shall come upon you for this.”

units.leftText: Then the woman said, “Whom shall I bring up to you?”
units.rightText: “Whom shall I bring up for you?” the woman asked.

units.rightText: But when the woman saw Samuel, she cried out in a loud voice and said to Saul, “Why have you deceived me? You are Saul!”

units.leftText: The king said to her, “Don’t be afraid! What do you see?”
units.rightText: “Do not be afraid,” the king replied. “What do you see?”

units.leftText: He said to her, “What does he look like?”
units.rightText: “What does he look like?” asked Saul.

units.leftText: Samuel said to Saul, “Why have you disturbed me, to bring me up?”
units.rightText: Then Samuel said to Saul, “Why have you disturbed me by bringing me up?”

units.leftText: Samuel said, “Why then do you ask me, since the LORD has departed from you and has become your adversary?
units.rightText: “Why do you consult me,” asked Samuel, “since the LORD has turned away from you and become your enemy?

units.rightText: Because you did not obey the LORD or carry out His burning anger against Amalek, the LORD has done this to you today.
